7.96.d: बृहदु गायिषे वचोऽसुर्या नदीनाम् । सरस्वतीमिन्महया सुवृक्तिभिः स्तोमैर्वसिष्ठ रोदसी ॥
7.96.e: I SING a lofty song, for she is mightiest, most divine of Streams.  Sarasvatī will I exalt with hymns and lauds, and, O Vasiṣṭha, Heaven and Earth.

7.96.d: उभे यत्ते महिना शुभ्रे अन्धसी अधिक्षियन्ति पूरवः । सा नो बोध्यवित्री मरुत्सखा चोद राधो मघोनाम् ॥
7.96.e: When in the fulness of their strength the Pūrus dwell, Beauteous One, on thy two grassy banks,  Favour us thou who hast the Maruts for thy friends: stir up the bounty of our chiefs.

7.96.d: भद्रमिद्भद्रा कृणवत्सरस्वत्यकवारी चेतति वाजिनीवती । गृणाना जमदग्निवत्स्तुवाना च वसिष्ठवत् ॥
7.96.e: So may Sarasvatī auspicious send good luck; she, rich in spoil, is never niggardly in thought,  When praised in jamadagni's way and lauded as Vasiṣṭha lauds.

7.96.d: जनीयन्तो न्वग्रवः पुत्रीयन्तः सुदानवः । सरस्वन्तं हवामहे ॥
7.96.e: We call upon Sarasvān, as unmarried men who long for wives,  As liberal men who yearn for sons.

7.96.d: ये ते सरस्व ऊर्मयो मधुमन्तो घृतश्चुतः । तेभिर्नोऽविता भव ॥
7.96.e: Be thou our kind protector, O Sarasvān, with those waves of thine  Laden with sweets and dropping oil.

7.96.d: पीपिवांसं सरस्वतः स्तनं यो विश्वदर्शतः । भक्षीमहि प्रजामिषम् ॥
7.96.e: May we enjoy Sarasvān's breast, all-beautiful, that swells with streams,  May we gain food and progeny.

7.97.d: यज्ञे दिवो नृषदने पृथिव्या नरो यत्र देवयवो मदन्ति । इन्द्राय यत्र सवनानि सुन्वे गमन्मदाय प्रथमं वयश्च ॥
7.97.e: WHERE Heaven and Earth combine in men's assembly, and ttose who love the Gods delight in worship,  Where the libations are effused for Indra, may he come first to drink and make him stronger.

7.97.d: आ दैव्या वृणीमहेऽवांसि बृहस्पतिर्नो मह आ सखायः । यथा भवेम मीळ्हुषे अनागा यो नो दाता परावतः पितेव ॥
7.97.e: We crave the heavenly grace of Gods to guard us-so may Bṛhaspati, O friends, exalt us-  That he, the Bounteous God, may find us sintess, who giveth from a distance like a father.

7.97.d: तमु ज्येष्ठं नमसा हविर्भिः सुशेवं ब्रह्मणस्पतिं गृणीषे । इन्द्रं श्लोको महि दैव्यः सिषक्तु यो ब्रह्मणो देवकृतस्य राजा ॥
7.97.e: That Brahmaṇaspati, most High and Gracious, I glorify with offerings and with homage.  May the great song of praise divine, reach Indra who is the King of prayer the Gods’ creation.

7.97.d: स आ नो योनिं सदतु प्रेष्ठो बृहस्पतिर्विश्ववारो यो अस्ति । कामो रायः सुवीर्यस्य तं दात्पर्षन्नो अति सश्चतो अरिष्टान् ॥
7.97.e: May that Bṛhaspati who brings all blessings, most dearly loved, be seated by our altar.  Heroes and wealth we crave; may he bestow them, and bear us safe beyond the men who vex us.

7.97.d: तमा नो अर्कममृताय जुष्टमिमे धासुरमृतासः पुराजाः । शुचिक्रन्दं यजतं पस्त्यानां बृहस्पतिमनर्वाणं हुवेम ॥
7.97.e: To us these Deathless Ones, erst born, have granted this laud of ours which gives the Immortal pleasure.  Let us invoke Bṛhaspati, the foeless, the clear-voiced God, the Holy One of households

7.97.d: तं शग्मासो अरुषासो अश्वा बृहस्पतिं सहवाहो वहन्ति । सहश्चिद्यस्य नीलवत्सधस्थं नभो न रूपमरुषं वसानाः ॥
7.97.e: Him, this Bṛhaspati, his red-hued horses, drawing together, full of strength, bring hither.  Robed in red colour like the cloud, they carry the Lord of Might whose friendship gives a dwelling.

7.97.d: स हि शुचिः शतपत्रः स शुन्ध्युर्हिरण्यवाशीरिषिरः स्वर्षाः । बृहस्पतिः स स्वावेश ऋष्वः पुरू सखिभ्य आसुतिं करिष्ठः ॥
7.97.e: For he is pure, with hundred wings, refulgent, with sword of gold, impetuous, winning sunlight.  Sublime Bṛhaspati, easy of access granteth his friends most bountiful refreshment.

7.97.d: देवी देवस्य रोदसी जनित्री बृहस्पतिं वावृधतुर्महित्वा । दक्षाय्याय दक्षता सखायः करद्ब्रह्मणे सुतरा सुगाधा ॥
7.97.e: Both Heaven and Earth, divine, the Deity's Parents, have made Bṛhaspati increase in grandeur.  Glorify him, O friends, who merits glory: may he give prayer fair way and easy passage.

7.97.d: इयं वां ब्रह्मणस्पते सुवृक्तिर्ब्रह्मेन्द्राय वज्रिणे अकारि । अविष्टं धियो जिगृतं पुरंधीर्जजस्तमर्यो वनुषामरातीः ॥
7.97.e: This, Brahmaṇaspati, is your laudation prayer hath been made to thunderwielding Indra.  Favour our songs, wake up our thought and spirit: destroy the godless and our foemen's malice.

7.97.d: बृहस्पते युवमिन्द्रश्च वस्वो दिव्यस्येशाथे उत पार्थिवस्य । धत्तं रयिं स्तुवते कीरये चिद्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.97.e: Ye Twain are Lords of wealth in earth and heaven, thou, O Bṛhaspati, and thou, O Indra.  Mean though he be, give wealth to him who lauds you. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.98.d: अध्वर्यवोऽरुणं दुग्धमंशुं जुहोतन वृषभाय क्षितीनाम् । गौराद्वेदीयाँ अवपानमिन्द्रो विश्वाहेद्याति सुतसोममिच्छन् ॥
7.98.e: PRIESTS, offer to the Lord of all the people the milked-out stalk of Soma, radiant-coloured.  No wild-bull knows his drinking-place like Indra who ever seeks him who hath pressed the Soma,

7.98.d: यद्दधिषे प्रदिवि चार्वन्नं दिवेदिवे पीतिमिदस्य वक्षि । उत हृदोत मनसा जुषाण उशन्निन्द्र प्रस्थितान्पाहि सोमान् ॥
7.98.e: Thou dost desire to drink, each day that passes, the pleasant food which thou hast had aforetime,  O Indra, gratified in heart and spirit, drink eagerly the Soma set before thee.

7.98.d: जज्ञानः सोमं सहसे पपाथ प्र ते माता महिमानमुवाच । एन्द्र पप्राथोर्व१न्तरिक्षं युधा देवेभ्यो वरिवश्चकर्थ ॥
7.98.e: Thou, newly-born, for strength didst drink the Soma; the Mother told thee of thy future greatness.  O Indra, thou hast filled mid-air's wide region, and given the Gods by battle room and freedom.

7.98.d: यद्योधया महतो मन्यमानान्त्साक्षाम तान्बाहुभिः शाशदानान् । यद्वा नृभिर्वृत इन्द्राभियुध्यास्तं त्वयाजिं सौश्रवसं जयेम ॥
7.98.e: When thou hast urged the arrocrant to combat, proud in their strength of arm, we will subdue them.  Or, Indra, when thou fightest girt by heroes, we in the glorious fray with thee will conquer.

7.98.d: प्रेन्द्रस्य वोचं प्रथमा कृतानि प्र नूतना मघवा या चकार । यदेददेवीरसहिष्ट माया अथाभवत्केवलः सोमो अस्य ॥
7.98.e: I will declare the earliest deeds of Indra, and recent acts which Maghavan hath accomplished.  When he had conquered godless wiles and magic, Soma became his own entire possession.

7.98.d: तवेदं विश्वमभितः पशव्यं१ यत्पश्यसि चक्षसा सूर्यस्य । गवामसि गोपतिरेक इन्द्र भक्षीमहि ते प्रयतस्य वस्वः ॥
7.98.e: Thine is this world of flocks and herds around thee, which with the eye of Sūrya thou beholdest.  Thou, Indra, art alone the Lord of cattle; may we enjoy the treasure which thou givest.

7.98.d: बृहस्पते युवमिन्द्रश्च वस्वो दिव्यस्येशाथे उत पार्थिवस्य । धत्तं रयिं स्तुवते कीरये चिद्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.98.e: Ye Twain are Lords of wealth in earth and heaven, thou, O Bṛhaspati, and thou, O Indra.  Mean though he be, give wealth to him who lauds you. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.99.d: परो मात्रया तन्वा वृधान न ते महित्वमन्वश्नुवन्ति । उभे ते विद्म रजसी पृथिव्या विष्णो देव त्वं परमस्य वित्से ॥
7.99.e: MEN come not nigh thy majesty who growest beyond all bound and measure with thy body.  Both thy two regions of the earth, O Viṣṇu, we know: thou God, knowest the highest also.

7.99.d: न ते विष्णो जायमानो न जातो देव महिम्नः परमन्तमाप । उदस्तभ्ना नाकमृष्वं बृहन्तं दाधर्थ प्राचीं ककुभं पृथिव्याः ॥
7.99.e: None who is born or being born, God Viṣṇu, hath reached the utmost limit of thy grandeur.  The vast high vault of heaven hast thou supported, and fixed earth's eastern pinnacle securely.

7.99.d: इरावती धेनुमती हि भूतं सूयवसिनी मनुषे दशस्या । व्यस्तभ्ना रोदसी विष्णवेते दाधर्थ पृथिवीमभितो मयूखैः ॥
7.99.e: Rich in sweet food be ye, and rich in milch-kine, with fertile pastures, fain to do men service.  Both these worlds, Viṣṇu, hast thou stayed asunder, and firmly fixed the earth with pegs around it.

7.99.d: उरुं यज्ञाय चक्रथुरु लोकं जनयन्ता सूर्यमुषासमग्निम् । दासस्य चिद्वृषशिप्रस्य माया जघ्नथुर्नरा पृतनाज्येषु ॥
7.99.e: Ye have made spacious room for sacrificing by generating Sūrya, Dawn, and Agni.  O Heroes, ye have conquered in your battles even the bull-jawed Dāsa's wiles and magic.

7.99.d: इन्द्राविष्णू दृंहिताः शम्बरस्य नव पुरो नवतिं च श्नथिष्टम् । शतं वर्चिनः सहस्रं च साकं हथो अप्रत्यसुरस्य वीरान् ॥
7.99.e: Ye have destroyed, thou, Indra, and thou Viṣṇu, Śambara's nine-and-ninety fenced castles.  Ye Twain smote down a hundred times a thousand resistless heroes of the royal Varcin.

7.99.d: इयं मनीषा बृहती बृहन्तोरुक्रमा तवसा वर्धयन्ती । ररे वां स्तोमं विदथेषु विष्णो पिन्वतमिषो वृजनेष्विन्द्र ॥
7.99.e: This is the lofty hymn of praise, exalting the Lords of Mighty Stride, the strong and lofty.  I laud you in the solemn synods, Viṣṇu: pour ye food on us in our camps, O Indra.

7.99.d: वषट् ते विष्णवास आ कृणोमि तन्मे जुषस्व शिपिविष्ट हव्यम् । वर्धन्तु त्वा सुष्टुतयो गिरो मे यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.99.e: O Viṣṇu, unto thee my lips cry Vaṣaṭ! Let this mine offering, Sipivista, please thee.  May these my songs of eulogy exalt thee. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.100.d: नू मर्तो दयते सनिष्यन्यो विष्णव उरुगायाय दाशत् । प्र यः सत्राचा मनसा यजात एतावन्तं नर्यमाविवासात् ॥
7.100.e: NE’ER doth the man repent, who, seeking profit, bringeth his gift to the far-striding Viṣṇu.  He who adoreth him with all his spirit winneth himself so great a benefactor.

7.100.d: त्वं विष्णो सुमतिं विश्वजन्यामप्रयुतामेवयावो मतिं दाः । पर्चो यथा नः सुवितस्य भूरेरश्वावतः पुरुश्चन्द्रस्य रायः ॥
7.100.e: Thou, Viṣṇu, constant in thy courses, gavest good-will to all men, and a hymn that lasteth,  That thou mightst move us to abundant comfort of very splendid wealth with store of horses.

7.100.d: त्रिर्देवः पृथिवीमेष एतां वि चक्रमे शतर्चसं महित्वा । प्र विष्णुरस्तु तवसस्तवीयान्त्वेषं ह्यस्य स्थविरस्य नाम ॥
7.100.e: Three times strode forth this God in all his grandeur over this earth bright with a hundred splendours.  Foremost be Viṣṇu, stronger than the strongest: for glorious is his name who lives for ever.

7.100.d: वि चक्रमे पृथिवीमेष एतां क्षेत्राय विष्णुर्मनुषे दशस्यन् । ध्रुवासो अस्य कीरयो जनास उरुक्षितिं सुजनिमा चकार ॥
7.100.e: Over this earth with mighty step strode Viṣṇu, ready to give it for a home to Manu.  In him the humble people trust for safety: he, nobly born, hath made them spacious dwellings.

7.100.d: प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट नामार्यः शंसामि वयुनानि विद्वान् । तं त्वा गृणामि तवसमतव्यान्क्षयन्तमस्य रजसः पराके ॥
7.100.e: To-day I laud this name, O gipivista, I, skilled in rules, the name of thee the Noble.  Yea, I the poor and weak praise thee the Mighty who dwellest in the realm beyond this region.

7.100.d: किमित्ते विष्णो परिचक्ष्यं भूत्प्र यद्ववक्षे शिपिविष्टो अस्मि । मा वर्पो अस्मदप गूह एतद्यदन्यरूपः समिथे बभूथ ॥
7.100.e: What was there to be blamed in thee, O Viṣṇu, when thou declaredst, I am Sipivista?  Hide not this form from us, nor keep it secret, since thou didst wear another shape in battle.

7.100.d: वषट् ते विष्णवास आ कृणोमि तन्मे जुषस्व शिपिविष्ट हव्यम् । वर्धन्तु त्वा सुष्टुतयो गिरो मे यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.100.e: O Viṣṇu, unto thee my lips cry Vaṣaṭ! Let this mine offering, Sipivista, please thee.  May these my songs of eulogy exalt thee. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.101.d: तिस्रो वाचः प्र वद ज्योतिरग्रा या एतद्दुह्रे मधुदोघमूधः । स वत्सं कृण्वन्गर्भमोषधीनां सद्यो जातो वृषभो रोरवीति ॥
7.101.e: SPEAK forth three words, the words which light precedeth, which milk this udder that produceth nectar.  Quickly made manifest, the Bull hath bellowed, engendering the germ of plants, the Infant.

7.101.d: यो वर्धन ओषधीनां यो अपां यो विश्वस्य जगतो देव ईशे । स त्रिधातु शरणं शर्म यंसत्त्रिवर्तु ज्योतिः स्वभिष्ट्य१स्मे ॥
7.101.e: Giver of growth to plants, the God who ruleth over the waters and all moving creatures,  Vouchsafe us triple shelter for our refuge, and threefold light to succour and befriend us.

7.101.d: स्तरीरु त्वद्भवति सूत उ त्वद्यथावशं तन्वं चक्र एषः । पितुः पयः प्रति गृभ्णाति माता तेन पिता वर्धते तेन पुत्रः ॥
7.101.e: Now he is sterile, now begetteth offspring, even as he willeth doth he change his figure.  The Father's genial flow bedews the Mother; therewith the Sire, therewith the son is nourished.

7.101.d: यस्मिन्विश्वानि भुवनानि तस्थुस्तिस्रो द्यावस्त्रेधा सस्रुरापः । त्रयः कोशास उपसेचनासो मध्वः श्चोतन्त्यभितो विरप्शम् ॥
7.101.e: In him all living creatures have their being, and the three heavens with triply-flowing waters.  Three reservoirs that sprinkle down their treasure shed their sweet streams around him with a murmur.

7.101.d: इदं वचः पर्जन्याय स्वराजे हृदो अस्त्वन्तरं तज्जुजोषत् । मयोभुवो वृष्टयः सन्त्वस्मे सुपिप्पला ओषधीर्देवगोपाः ॥
7.101.e: May this my song to Sovran Lord Parjanya come near unto his heart and give him pleasure.  May we obtain the showers that bring enjoyment, and God-protected plants with goodly fruitage.

7.101.d: स रेतोधा वृषभः शश्वतीनां तस्मिन्नात्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च । तन्म ऋतं पातु शतशारदाय यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.101.e: He is the Bull of all, and their impregner: he holds the life of all things fixed and moving.  May this rite save me till my hundredth autumn. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.102.d: पर्जन्याय प्र गायत दिवस्पुत्राय मीळ्हुषे । स नो यवसमिच्छतु ॥
7.102.e: SING forth and laud Parjanya, son of Heaven, who sends the gift of rain  May he provide our pasturage.

7.102.d: यो गर्भमोषधीनां गवां कृणोत्यर्वताम् । पर्जन्यः पुरुषीणाम् ॥
7.102.e: Parjanya is the God who forms in kine, in mares, in plants of earth,  And womankind, the germ of life.

7.102.d: तस्मा इदास्ये हविर्जुहोता मधुमत्तमम् । इळां नः संयतं करत् ॥
7.102.e: Offer and pour into his mouth oblation rich in savoury juice:  May he for ever give us food.

7.103.d: संवत्सरं शशयाना ब्राह्मणा व्रतचारिणः । वाचं पर्जन्यजिन्वितां प्र मण्डूका अवादिषुः ॥
7.103.e: THEY who lay quiet for a year, the Brahmans who fulfil their vows,  The Frogs have lifted up their voice, the voice Parjanya hath inspired.

7.103.d: दिव्या आपो अभि यदेनमायन्दृतिं न शुष्कं सरसी शयानम् । गवामह न मायुर्वत्सिनीनां मण्डूकानां वग्नुरत्रा समेति ॥
7.103.e: What time on these, as on a dry skin lying in the pool's bed, the floods of heaven descended,  The music of the Frogs comes forth in concert like the cows lowing with their calves beside them.

7.103.d: यदीमेनाँ उशतो अभ्यवर्षीत्तृष्यावतः प्रावृष्यागतायाम् । अख्खलीकृत्या पितरं न पुत्रो अन्यो अन्यमुप वदन्तमेति ॥
7.103.e: When at the coming of the Rains the water has poured upon them as they yearned and thirsted,  One seeks another as he talks and greets him with cries of pleasure as a son his father.

7.103.d: अन्यो अन्यमनु गृभ्णात्येनोरपां प्रसर्गे यदमन्दिषाताम् । मण्डूको यदभिवृष्टः कनिष्कन्पृश्निः सम्पृङ्क्ते हरितेन वाचम् ॥
7.103.e: Each of these twain receives the other kindly, while they are revelling in the flow of waters,  When the Frog moistened by the rain springs forward, and Green and Spotty both combine their voices.

7.103.d: यदेषामन्यो अन्यस्य वाचं शाक्तस्येव वदति शिक्षमाणः । सर्वं तदेषां समृधेव पर्व यत्सुवाचो वदथनाध्यप्सु ॥
7.103.e: When one of these repeats the other's language, as he who learns the lesson of the teacher,  Your every limb seems to be growing larger as ye converse with eloquence on the waters.

7.103.d: गोमायुरेको अजमायुरेकः पृश्निरेको हरित एक एषाम् । समानं नाम बिभ्रतो विरूपाः पुरुत्रा वाचं पिपिशुर्वदन्तः ॥
7.103.e: Onc is Cow-bellow and Goat-bleat the other, one Frog is Green and one of them is Spotty.  They bear one common name, and yet they vary, and, talking, modulate the voice diversely.

7.103.d: ब्राह्मणासो अतिरात्रे न सोमे सरो न पूर्णमभितो वदन्तः । संवत्सरस्य तदहः परि ष्ठ यन्मण्डूकाः प्रावृषीणं बभूव ॥
7.103.e: As Brahmans, sitting round the brimful vessel, talk at the Soma-rite of Atiratra,  So, Frogs, ye gather round the pool to honour this day of all the year, the first of Rain-time.

7.103.d: ब्राह्मणासः सोमिनो वाचमक्रत ब्रह्म कृण्वन्तः परिवत्सरीणम् । अध्वर्यवो घर्मिणः सिष्विदाना आविर्भवन्ति गुह्या न के चित् ॥
7.103.e: These Brahmans with the Soma juice, performing their year-long rite, have lifted up their voices;  And these Adhvaryus, sweating with their kettles, come forth and show themselves, and none are hidden.

7.103.d: देवहितिं जुगुपुर्द्वादशस्य ऋतुं नरो न प्र मिनन्त्येते । संवत्सरे प्रावृष्यागतायां तप्ता घर्मा अश्नुवते विसर्गम् ॥
7.103.e: They keep the twelve month's God-appointed order, and never do the men neglect the season.  Soon as the Rain-time in the year returneth, these who were heated kettles gain their freedom.

7.103.d: गोमायुरदादजमायुरदात्पृश्निरदाद्धरितो नो वसूनि । गवां मण्डूका ददतः शतानि सहस्रसावे प्र तिरन्त आयुः ॥
7.103.e: Cow-bellow and Goat-bleat have granted riches, and Green and Spotty have vouchsafed us treasure.  The Frogs who give us cows in hundreds lengthen our lives in this most fertilizing season.

7.104.d: इन्द्रासोमा तपतं रक्ष उब्जतं न्यर्पयतं वृषणा तमोवृधः । परा शृणीतमचितो न्योषतं हतं नुदेथां नि शिशीतमत्रिणः ॥
7.104.e: INDRA and Soma, burn, destroy the demon foe, send downward, O ye Bulls, those who add gloom to gloom.  Annihilate the fools, slay them and burn them up: chase them away from us, pierce the voracious ones.

7.104.d: इन्द्रासोमा समघशंसमभ्य१घं तपुर्ययस्तु चरुरग्निवाँ इव । ब्रह्मद्विषे क्रव्यादे घोरचक्षसे द्वेषो धत्तमनवायं किमीदिने ॥
7.104.e: Indra and Soma, let sin round the wicked boil like as a caldron set amid the flames of fire.  Against the foe of prayer, devourer of raw flesh, the vile fiend fierce of eye, keep ye perpetual hate.

7.104.d: इन्द्रासोमा दुष्कृतो वव्रे अन्तरनारम्भणे तमसि प्र विध्यतम् । यथा नातः पुनरेकश्चनोदयत्तद्वामस्तु सहसे मन्युमच्छवः ॥
7.104.e: Indra and Soma, plunge the wicked in the depth, yea, cast them into darkness that hath no support,  So that not one of them may ever thence return: so may your wrathful might prevail and conquer them.

7.104.d: इन्द्रासोमा वर्तयतं दिवो वधं सं पृथिव्या अघशंसाय तर्हणम् । उत्तक्षतं स्वर्यं१ पर्वतेभ्यो येन रक्षो वावृधानं निजूर्वथः ॥
7.104.e: Indra and Soma, hurl your deadly crushing bolt down on the wicked fiend from heaven and from the earth.  Yea, forge out of the mountains your celestial dart wherewith ye burn to death the waxing demon race.

7.104.d: इन्द्रासोमा वर्तयतं दिवस्पर्यग्नितप्तेभिर्युवमश्महन्मभिः । तपुर्वधेभिरजरेभिरत्रिणो नि पर्शाने विध्यतं यन्तु निस्वरम् ॥
7.104.e: Indra and Soma, cast ye downward out of heaven your deadly darts of stone burning with fiery flame,  Eternal, scorching darts; plunge the voracious ones within the depth, and let them sink without a sound.

7.104.d: इन्द्रासोमा परि वां भूतु विश्वत इयं मतिः कक्ष्याश्वेव वाजिना । यां वां होत्रां परिहिनोमि मेधयेमा ब्रह्माणि नृपतीव जिन्वतम् ॥
7.104.e: Indra and Soma, let this hymn control you both, even as the girth encompasses two vigorous steeds-  The song of praise which I with wisdom offer you: do ye, as Lords of men, animate these my prayers.

7.104.d: प्रति स्मरेथां तुजयद्भिरेवैर्हतं द्रुहो रक्षसो भङ्गुरावतः । इन्द्रासोमा दुष्कृते मा सुगं भूद्यो नः कदा चिदभिदासति द्रुहा ॥
7.104.e: In your impetuous manner think ye both thereon: destroy these evil beings, slay the treacherous fiends.  Indra and Soma, let the wicked have no bliss who evermore assails us with malignity.

7.104.d: यो मा पाकेन मनसा चरन्तमभिचष्टे अनृतेभिर्वचोभिः । आप इव काशिना संगृभीता असन्नस्त्वासत इन्द्र वक्ता ॥
7.104.e: Whoso accuses me with words of falsehood when I pursue my way with guileless spirit,  May he, the speaker of untruth, be, Indra, like water which the hollowed hand compresses.

7.104.d: ये पाकशंसं विहरन्त एवैर्ये वा भद्रं दूषयन्ति स्वधाभिः । अहये वा तान्प्रददातु सोम आ वा दधातु निर्ऋतेरुपस्थे ॥
7.104.e: Those who destroy, as is their wont, the simple, and with their evil natures barm the righteous,  May Soma give them over to the serpent, or to the lap of Nirrti consign them.

7.104.d: यो नो रसं दिप्सति पित्वो अग्ने यो अश्वानां यो गवां यस्तनूनाम् । रिपुः स्तेनः स्तेयकृद्दभ्रमेतु नि ष हीयतां तन्वा३ तना च ॥
7.104.e: The fiend, O Agni, who designs to injure the essence of our food, kine, steeds, or bodies,  May he, the adversary, thief, and robber, sink to destruction, both himself and offipring.

7.104.d: परः सो अस्तु तन्वा३ तना च तिस्रः पृथिवीरधो अस्तु विश्वाः । प्रति शुष्यतु यशो अस्य देवा यो नो दिवा दिप्सति यश्च नक्तम् ॥
7.104.e: May he be swept away, himself and children: may all the three earths press him down beneath them.  May his fair glory, O ye Gods, be blighted, who in the day or night would fain destroy us.

7.104.d: सुविज्ञानं चिकितुषे जनाय सच्चासच्च वचसी पस्पृधाते । तयोर्यत्सत्यं यतरदृजीयस्तदित्सोमोऽवति हन्त्यासत् ॥
7.104.e: The prudent finds it easy to distinguish the true and false: their words oppose each other.  Of these two that which is the true and honest, Soma protects, and brings the false to nothing.

7.104.d: न वा उ सोमो वृजिनं हिनोति न क्षत्रियं मिथुया धारयन्तम् । हन्ति रक्षो हन्त्यासद्वदन्तमुभाविन्द्रस्य प्रसितौ शयाते ॥
7.104.e: Never doth Soma aid and guide the wicked or him who falsely claims the Warrior's title.  He slays the fiend and him who speaks untruly: both lie entangled in the noose of Indra.

7.104.d: यदि वाहमनृतदेव आस मोघं वा देवाँ अप्यूहे अग्ने । किमस्मभ्यं जातवेदो हृणीषे द्रोघवाचस्ते निर्ऋथं सचन्ताम् ॥
7.104.e: As if I worshipped deities of falsehood, or thought vain thoughts about the Gods, O Agni.  Why art thou angry with us, Jātavedas? Destruction fall on those who lie against thee!

7.104.d: अद्या मुरीय यदि यातुधानो अस्मि यदि वायुस्ततप पूरुषस्य । अधा स वीरैर्दशभिर्वि यूया यो मा मोघं यातुधानेत्याह ॥
7.104.e: So may I die this day if I have harassed any man's life or if I be a demon.  Yea, may he lose all his ten sons together who with false tongue hath called me Yātudhāna.

7.104.d: यो मायातुं यातुधानेत्याह यो वा रक्षाः शुचिरस्मीत्याह । इन्द्रस्तं हन्तु महता वधेन विश्वस्य जन्तोरधमस्पदीष्ट ॥
7.104.e: May Indra slay him with a mighty weapon, and let the vilest of all creatures perish,  The fiend who says that he is pure, who calls me a demon though devoid of demon nature.

7.104.d: प्र या जिगाति खर्गलेव नक्तमप द्रुहा तन्वं१ गूहमाना । वव्राँ अनन्ताँ अव सा पदीष्ट ग्रावाणो घ्नन्तु रक्षस उपब्दैः ॥
7.104.e: She too who wanders like an owl at night-time, hiding her body in her guile and malice,  May she fall downward into endless caverns. May press-stones with loud ring destroy the demons.

7.104.d: वि तिष्ठध्वं मरुतो विक्ष्वि१च्छत गृभायत रक्षसः सं पिनष्टन । वयो ये भूत्वी पतयन्ति नक्तभिर्ये वा रिपो दधिरे देवे अध्वरे ॥
7.104.e: Spread out, ye Maruts, search among the people: seize ye and grind the Rākṣasas to pieces,  Who fly abroad, transformed to birds, at night-time, or sully and pollute our holy worship.

7.104.d: प्र वर्तय दिवो अश्मानमिन्द्र सोमशितं मघवन्त्सं शिशाधि । प्राक्तादपाक्तादधरादुदक्तादभि जहि रक्षसः पर्वतेन ॥
7.104.e: Hurl down from heaven thy bolt of stone, O Indra: sharpen it, Maghavan, made keen by Soma.  Forward, behind, and from above and under, smite down the demons with thy rocky weapon.

7.104.d: एत उ त्ये पतयन्ति श्वयातव इन्द्रं दिप्सन्ति दिप्सवोऽदाभ्यम् । शिशीते शक्रः पिशुनेभ्यो वधं नूनं सृजदशनिं यातुमद्भ्यः ॥
7.104.e: They fly, the demon dogs, and, bent on mischief, fain would they harm indomitable Indra.  Śakra makes sharp his weapon for the wicked: now, let him cast his bolt at fiendish wizards.

7.104.d: इन्द्रो यातूनामभवत्पराशरो हविर्मथीनामभ्या३विवासताम् । अभीदु शक्रः परशुर्यथा वनं पात्रेव भिन्दन्त्सत एति रक्षसः ॥
7.104.e: Indra hath ever been the fiends’ destroyer who spoil oblations of the Gods’ invokers:  Yea, Śakra, like an axe that  splits  the timber, attacks and smashes them like earthen vessels.

7.104.d: उलूकयातुं शुशुलूकयातुं जहि श्वयातुमुत कोकयातुम् । सुपर्णयातुमुत गृध्रयातुं दृषदेव प्र मृण रक्ष इन्द्र ॥
7.104.e: Destroy the fiend shaped like an owl or owlet, destroy him in the form of dog or cuckoo.  Destroy him shaped as eagle or as vulture as with a stone, O Indra, crush the demon.

7.104.d: मा नो रक्षो अभि नड्यातुमावतामपोच्छतु मिथुना या किमीदिना । पृथिवी नः पार्थिवात्पात्वंहसोऽन्तरिक्षं दिव्यात्पात्वस्मान् ॥
7.104.e: Let not the fiend of witchcraft-workers reach us: may Dawn drive off the couples of Kimīdins.  Earth keep us safe from earthly woe and trouble: from grief that comes from heaven mid-air preserve us.

7.104.d: इन्द्र जहि पुमांसं यातुधानमुत स्त्रियं मायया शाशदानाम् । विग्रीवासो मूरदेवा ऋदन्तु मा ते दृशन्त्सूर्यमुच्चरन्तम् ॥
7.104.e: Slay the male demon, Indra! slay the female, joying and triumphing in arts of magic.  Let the fools' gods with bent necks fall and perish, and see no more the Sun when he arises.

7.104.d: प्रति चक्ष्व वि चक्ष्वेन्द्रश्च सोम जागृतम् । रक्षोभ्यो वधमस्यतमशनिं यातुमद्भ्यः ॥
7.104.e: Look each one hither, look around Indra and Soma, watch ye well. Cast forth your weapon at the fiends against the sorcerers hurt your bolt.

8.1.d: मा चिदन्यद्वि शंसत सखायो मा रिषण्यत । इन्द्रमित्स्तोता वृषणं सचा सुते मुहुरुक्था च शंसत ॥
8.1.e: GLORIFY naught besides, O friends; so shall no sorrow trouble you.  Praise only mighty Indra when the juice is shed, and say your lauds repeatedly:

8.1.d: अवक्रक्षिणं वृषभं यथाजुरं गां न चर्षणीसहम् । विद्वेषणं संवननोभयंकरं मंहिष्ठमुभयाविनम् ॥
8.1.e: Even him, eternal, like a bull who rushes down, men's Conqueror, bounteous like a cow;  Him who is cause of both, of enmity and peace, to both sides most munificent.

8.1.d: यच्चिद्धि त्वा जना इमे नाना हवन्त ऊतये । अस्माकं ब्रह्मेदमिन्द्र भूतु तेऽहा विश्वा च वर्धनम् ॥
8.1.e: Although these men in sundry ways invoke thee to obtain thine aid,  Be this our prayer, addressed, O Indra, unto thee, thine exaltation every day.

8.1.d: वि तर्तूर्यन्ते मघवन्विपश्चितोऽर्यो विपो जनानाम् । उप क्रमस्व पुरुरूपमा भर वाजं नेदिष्ठमूतये ॥
8.1.e: Those skilled in song, O Maghavan among these men o’ercome with might the foeman's songs.  Come hither, bring us strength in many a varied form most near that it may succour us.

8.1.d: महे चन त्वामद्रिवः परा शुल्काय देयाम् । न सहस्राय नायुताय वज्रिवो न शताय शतामघ ॥
8.1.e: O Caster of the Stone, I would not sell thee for a mighty price,  Not for a thousand, Thunderer! nor ten thousand, nor a hundred, Lord of countless wealth!

8.1.d: वस्याँ इन्द्रासि मे पितुरुत भ्रातुरभुञ्जतः । माता च मे छदयथः समा वसो वसुत्वनाय राधसे ॥
8.1.e: O Indra, thou art more to me than sire or niggard brother is.  Thou and my mother, O Good Lord, appear alike, to give me wealth abundantly.

8.1.d: क्वेयथ क्वेदसि पुरुत्रा चिद्धि ते मनः । अलर्षि युध्म खजकृत्पुरंदर प्र गायत्रा अगासिषुः ॥
8.1.e: Where art thou? Whither art thou gone? For many a place attracts thy mind.  Haste, Warrior, Fort-destroyer, Lord of battle's din, haste, holy songs have sounded forth.

8.1.d: प्रास्मै गायत्रमर्चत वावातुर्यः पुरंदरः । याभिः काण्वस्योप बर्हिरासदं यासद्वज्री भिनत्पुरः ॥
8.1.e: Sing out the psalm to him who breaks down castles for his faithful friend,  Verses to bring the Thunderer to destroy the forts and sit on Kaṇva's sacred grass.

8.1.d: ये ते सन्ति दशग्विनः शतिनो ये सहस्रिणः । अश्वासो ये ते वृषणो रघुद्रुवस्तेभिर्नस्तूयमा गहि ॥
8.1.e: The Horses which are thine in tens, in hundreds, yea, in thousands thine,  Even those vigorous Steeds, fleet-footed in the course, with those come quickly near to us.

8.1.d: आ त्व१द्य सबर्दुघां हुवे गायत्रवेपसम् । इन्द्रं धेनुं सुदुघामन्यामिषमुरुधारामरंकृतम् ॥
8.1.e: This day I call Sabardughā who animates the holy song,  Indra the richly-yielding Milch-cow who provides unfailing food in ample stream.

8.1.d: यत्तुदत्सूर एतशं वङ्कू वातस्य पर्णिना । वहत्कुत्समार्जुनेयं शतक्रतुः त्सरद्गन्धर्वमस्तृतम् ॥
8.1.e: When Sūra wounded Etaśa, with Vāta's rolling winged car.  Indra bore Kutsa Ārjuneya off, and mocked Gandharva. the unconquered One.

8.1.d: य ऋते चिदभिश्रिषः पुरा जत्रुभ्य आतृदः । संधाता संधिं मघवा पुरूवसुरिष्कर्ता विह्रुतं पुनः ॥
8.1.e: He without ligature, before making incision in the neck,  Closed up the wound again, most wealthy Maghavan, who maketh whole the injured part.

8.1.d: मा भूम निष्ट्या इवेन्द्र त्वदरणा इव । वनानि न प्रजहितान्यद्रिवो दुरोषासो अमन्महि ॥
8.1.e: May we be never cast aside, and strangers, as it were, to thee.  We, Thunder-wielding Indra, count ourselves as trees rejected and unfit to burn.

8.1.d: अमन्महीदनाशवोऽनुग्रासश्च वृत्रहन् । सकृत्सु ते महता शूर राधसा अनु स्तोमं मुदीमहि ॥
8.1.e: O Vṛtra-slayer, we were thought slow and unready for the fray.  Yet once in thy great bounty may we have delight, O Hero, after praising thee.

8.1.d: यदि स्तोमं मम श्रवदस्माकमिन्द्रमिन्दवः । तिरः पवित्रं ससृवांस आशवो मन्दन्तु तुग्र्यावृधः ॥
8.1.e: If he will listen to my laud, then may out Soma-drops that flow  Rapidly through the strainer gladden Indra, drops due to the Tugryas’ Strengthener.

8.1.d: आ त्व१द्य सधस्तुतिं वावातुः सख्युरा गहि । उपस्तुतिर्मघोनां प्र त्वावत्वधा ते वश्मि सुष्टुतिम् ॥
8.1.e: Come now unto the common laud of thee and of thy faithful friend.  So may our wealthy nobles’ praise give joy to thee. Fain would I sing thine eulogy.

8.1.d: सोता हि सोममद्रिभिरेमेनमप्सु धावत । गव्या वस्त्रेव वासयन्त इन्नरो निर्धुक्षन्वक्षणाभ्यः ॥
8.1.e: Press out the Soma with the stones, and in the waters wash it clean.  The men investing it with raiment made of milk shall milk it forth from out the stems.

8.1.d: अध ज्मो अध वा दिवो बृहतो रोचनादधि । अया वर्धस्व तन्वा गिरा ममा जाता सुक्रतो पृण ॥
8.1.e: Whether thou come from earth or from the lustre of the lofty heaven,  Wax stronger in thy body through my song of praise: fill full all creatures, O most Wise.

8.1.d: इन्द्राय सु मदिन्तमं सोमं सोता वरेण्यम् । शक्र एणं पीपयद्विश्वया धिया हिन्वानं न वाजयुम् ॥
8.1.e: For India press the Soma out, most gladdening and most excellent.  May Śakra make it swell sent forth with every prayer and asking, as it were, for strength.

8.1.d: मा त्वा सोमस्य गल्दया सदा याचन्नहं गिरा । भूर्णिं मृगं न सवनेषु चुक्रुधं क ईशानं न याचिषत् ॥
8.1.e: Let me not, still beseeching thee with earnest song at Soma rites,  Anger thee like  some  wild beast. Who would not beseech him who hath power to grant his prayer?

8.1.d: मदेनेषितं मदमुग्रमुग्रेण शवसा । विश्वेषां तरुतारं मदच्युतं मदे हि ष्मा ददाति नः ॥
8.1.e: The draught made swift with rapturous joy, effectual with its mighty strength,  All-conquering, distilling transport, let him drink: for he in ecstasy gives us gifts.

8.1.d: शेवारे वार्या पुरु देवो मर्ताय दाशुषे । स सुन्वते च स्तुवते च रासते विश्वगूर्तो अरिष्टुतः ॥
8.1.e: Where bliss is not, may he, All-praised, God whom the pious glorify,  Bestow great wealth upon the mortal worshipper who sheds the juice and praises him.

8.1.d: एन्द्र याहि मत्स्व चित्रेण देव राधसा । सरो न प्रास्युदरं सपीतिभिरा सोमेभिरुरु स्फिरम् ॥
8.1.e: Come, Indra, and rejoice thyself, O God, in manifold affluence.  Thou fillest like a lake thy vast capacious bulk with Soma and with draughts besides.

8.1.d: आ त्वा सहस्रमा शतं युक्ता रथे हिरण्यये । ब्रह्मयुजो हरय इन्द्र केशिनो वहन्तु सोमपीतये ॥
8.1.e: A thousand and a hundred Steeds are harnessed to thy golden car.  So may the long-maned Bays, yoked by devotion, bring Indra to drink the Soma juice.

8.1.d: आ त्वा रथे हिरण्यये हरी मयूरशेप्या । शितिपृष्ठा वहतां मध्वो अन्धसो विवक्षणस्य पीतये ॥
8.1.e: Yoked to thy chariot wrought of gold, may thy two Bays with peacock tails,  Convey thee hither, Steeds with their white backs, to quaff sweet juice that makes us eloquent.

8.1.d: पिबा त्व१स्य गिर्वणः सुतस्य पूर्वपा इव । परिष्कृतस्य रसिन इयमासुतिश्चारुर्मदाय पत्यते ॥
8.1.e: So drink, thou Lover of the Song, as the first drinker, of this juice.  This the outpouring of the savoury sap prepared is good and meet to gladden thee.

8.1.d: य एको अस्ति दंसना महाँ उग्रो अभि व्रतैः । गमत्स शिप्री न स योषदा गमद्धवं न परि वर्जति ॥
8.1.e: He who alone by wondrous deed is Mighty, Strong by holy works,  May he come, fair of cheek; may he not stay afar, but come and turn not from our call.

8.1.d: त्वं पुरं चरिष्ण्वं वधैः शुष्णस्य सं पिणक् । त्वं भा अनु चरो अध द्विता यदिन्द्र हव्यो भुवः ॥
8.1.e: Śuṣṇa's quick moving castle thou hast crushed to pieces with thy bolts.  Thou, Indra, from of old, hast followed after light, since we have had thee to invoke.

8.1.d: मम त्वा सूर उदिते मम मध्यंदिने दिवः । मम प्रपित्वे अपिशर्वरे वसवा स्तोमासो अवृत्सत ॥
8.1.e: My praises when the Sun hath risen, my praises at the time of noon,  My praises at the coming of the gloom of night, O Vasu, have gone forth to thee.

8.1.d: स्तुहि स्तुहीदेते घा ते मंहिष्ठासो मघोनाम् । निन्दिताश्वः प्रपथी परमज्या मघस्य मेध्यातिथे ॥
8.1.e: Praise yea, praise him. Of princes these are the most liberal of their gifts,  These, Paramajyā, Ninditāśva, Prapathī, most bounteous, O Medhyātithi.

8.1.d: आ यदश्वान्वनन्वतः श्रद्धयाहं रथे रुहम् । उत वामस्य वसुनश्चिकेतति यो अस्ति याद्वः पशुः ॥
8.1.e: When to the car, by faith, I yoked the horses longing for the way-  For skilled is Yadu's son in dealing precious wealth, he who is rich in herds of kine.

8.1.d: य ऋज्रा मह्यं मामहे सह त्वचा हिरण्यया । एष विश्वान्यभ्यस्तु सौभगासङ्गस्य स्वनद्रथः ॥
8.1.e: May he who gave me two brown steeds together with their cloths of gold,  May he, Āsaṅga's son Svanadratha, obtain all joy and high felicities.

8.1.d: अध प्लायोगिरति दासदन्यानासङ्गो अग्ने दशभिः सहस्रैः । अधोक्षणो दश मह्यं रुशन्तो नळा इव सरसो निरतिष्ठन् ॥
8.1.e: Playoga's son Āsaṅga, by ten thousand, O Agni, hath surpassed the rest in giving.  For me ten bright-hued oxen have come forward like lotus-stalks from out a lake upstanding.

8.1.d: अन्वस्य स्थूरं ददृशे पुरस्तादनस्थ ऊरुरवरम्बमाणः । शश्वती नार्यभिचक्ष्याह सुभद्रमर्य भोजनं बिभर्षि ॥
8.1.e: What time her husband's perfect restoration to his lost strength and manhood was apparent,  His consort Śaśvatī with joy addressed him, Now art thou well, my lord, and shalt be happy.

8.2.d: इदं वसो सुतमन्धः पिबा सुपूर्णमुदरम् । अनाभयिन्ररिमा ते ॥
8.2.e: HERE is the Soma juice expressed; O Vasu, drink till thou art full:  Undaunted God, we give it thee.

8.2.d: नृभिर्धूतः सुतो अश्नैरव्यो वारैः परिपूतः । अश्वो न निक्तो नदीषु ॥
8.2.e: Washed by the men, pressed out with stones, strained through the filter made of wool,  ’Tis like a courser bathed in stream.

8.2.d: तं ते यवं यथा गोभिः स्वादुमकर्म श्रीणन्तः । इन्द्र त्वास्मिन्त्सधमादे ॥
8.2.e: This juice have we made sweet for thee like barley, blending it with milk.  Indra, I call thee to our feast.

8.2.d: इन्द्र इत्सोमपा एक इन्द्रः सुतपा विश्वायुः । अन्तर्देवान्मर्त्याँश्च ॥
8.2.e: Beloved of all, Indra alone drinks up the flowing Soma juice  Among the Gods and mortal men.

8.2.d: न यं शुक्रो न दुराशीर्न तृप्रा उरुव्यचसम् । अपस्पृण्वते सुहार्दम् ॥
8.2.e: The Friend, whom not the brilliant-hued, the badly-mixt or bitter draught,  Repels, the far-extending God;

8.2.d: गोभिर्यदीमन्ये अस्मन्मृगं न व्रा मृगयन्ते । अभित्सरन्ति धेनुभिः ॥
8.2.e: While other men than we with milk chase him as hunters chase a deer,  And with their kine inveigle him.

8.2.d: त्रय इन्द्रस्य सोमाः सुतासः सन्तु देवस्य । स्वे क्षये सुतपाव्नः ॥
8.2.e: For him, for Indra, for the God, be pressed three draughts of Soma juice  In the juice-drinker's own abode.

8.2.d: त्रयः कोशासः श्चोतन्ति तिस्रश्चम्व१ः सुपूर्णाः । समाने अधि भार्मन् ॥
8.2.e: Three reservoirs exude their drops, filled are three beakers to the brim,  All for one offering to the God.

8.2.d: शुचिरसि पुरुनिःष्ठाः क्षीरैर्मध्यत आशीर्तः । दध्ना मन्दिष्ठः शूरस्य ॥
8.2.e: Pure art thou, set in many a place, and blended in the midst with milk  And curd, to cheer the Hero best.

8.2.d: इमे त इन्द्र सोमास्तीव्रा अस्मे सुतासः । शुक्रा आशिरं याचन्ते ॥
8.2.e: Here, Indra, are thy Soma-draughts pressed out by us, the strong, the pure:  They crave admixture of the milk.

8.2.d: ताँ आशिरं पुरोळाशमिन्द्रेमं सोमं श्रीणीहि । रेवन्तं हि त्वा शृणोमि ॥
8.2.e: O Indra, pour in milk, prepare the cake, and mix the Soma-draught.  I hear them say that thou art rich.

8.2.d: हृत्सु पीतासो युध्यन्ते दुर्मदासो न सुरायाम् । ऊधर्न नग्ना जरन्ते ॥
8.2.e: Quaffed juices fight within the breast. The drunken praise not by their wine,  The naked praise not when it rains.

8.2.d: रेवाँ इद्रेवतः स्तोता स्यात्त्वावतो मघोनः । प्रेदु हरिवः श्रुतस्य ॥
8.2.e: Rich be the praiser of one rich, munificent and famed like thee:  High rank be his, O Lord of Bays.

8.2.d: उक्थं चन शस्यमानमगोररिरा चिकेत । न गायत्रं गीयमानम् ॥
8.2.e: Foe of the man who adds no milk, he heeds not any chanted hymn  Or holy psalm that may he sung.

8.2.d: मा न इन्द्र पीयत्नवे मा शर्धते परा दाः । शिक्षा शचीवः शचीभिः ॥
8.2.e: Give us not, Indra, as a prey unto the scornful or the proud:  Help, Mighty One, with power and might.

8.2.d: वयमु त्वा तदिदर्था इन्द्र त्वायन्तः सखायः । कण्वा उक्थेभिर्जरन्ते ॥
8.2.e: This, even this, O Indra, we implore. as thy devoted friends,  The Kaṇvas praise thee with their hymns.

8.2.d: न घेमन्यदा पपन वज्रिन्नपसो नविष्टौ । तवेदु स्तोमं चिकेत ॥
8.2.e: Naught else, O Thunderer, have I praised in the skilled singer's eulogy:  On thy land only have I thought.

8.2.d: इच्छन्ति देवाः सुन्वन्तं न स्वप्नाय स्पृहयन्ति । यन्ति प्रमादमतन्द्राः ॥
8.2.e: The Gods seek him who presses out the Soma; they desire not sleep  They punish sloth unweariedly.

8.2.d: ओ षु प्र याहि वाजेभिर्मा हृणीथा अभ्य१स्मान् । महाँ इव युवजानिः ॥
8.2.e: Come hither swift with gifts of wealth - be not thou angry with us-like  A great man with a youthful bride.

8.2.d: मो ष्व१द्य दुर्हणावान्त्सायं करदारे अस्मत् । अश्रीर इव जामाता ॥
8.2.e: Let him not, wrathful with us, spend the evening far from us to-day,  Like some unpleasant son-in-law.

8.2.d: विद्मा ह्यस्य वीरस्य भूरिदावरीं सुमतिम् । त्रिषु जातस्य मनांसि ॥
8.2.e: For well we know this Hero's love, most liberal of the boons he gives,  His plans whom the three worlds display.

8.2.d: आ तू षिञ्च कण्वमन्तं न घा विद्म शवसानात् । यशस्तरं शतमूतेः ॥
8.2.e: Pour forth the gift which Kaṇvas bring, for none more glorious do we know  Than the Strong Lord with countless aids.

8.2.d: ज्येष्ठेन सोतरिन्द्राय सोमं वीराय शक्राय । भरा पिबन्नर्याय ॥
8.2.e: O presser, offer Soma first to Indra, Hero, Śakra, him  The Friend of man, that he may drink;

8.2.d: यो वेदिष्ठो अव्यथिष्वश्वावन्तं जरितृभ्यः । वाजं स्तोतृभ्यो गोमन्तम् ॥
8.2.e: Who, in untroubled ways, is best provider, for his worshippers.  Of strength in horses and in kine.

8.2.d: पन्यम्पन्यमित्सोतार आ धावत मद्याय । सोमं वीराय शूराय ॥
8.2.e: Pressers, for him blend Soma juice, each draught most excellent, for him  The Brave, the Hero, for his joy.

8.2.d: पाता वृत्रहा सुतमा घा गमन्नारे अस्मत् । नि यमते शतमूतिः ॥
8.2.e: The Vṛtra-slayer drinks the juice. May he who gives a hundred aids  Approach, nor stay afar from us.

8.2.d: एह हरी ब्रह्मयुजा शग्मा वक्षतः सखायम् । गीर्भिः श्रुतं गिर्वणसम् ॥
8.2.e: May the strong Bay Steeds, yoked by prayer, bring hither unto us our Friend,  Lover of Song, renowned by songs.

8.2.d: स्वादवः सोमा आ याहि श्रीताः सोमा आ याहि । शिप्रिन्नृषीवः शचीवो नायमच्छा सधमादम् ॥
8.2.e: Sweet are the Soma juices, come! Blent are the Soma juices, come!  Ṛṣi-like, mighty, fair of cheek, come hither quickly to the feast.

8.2.d: स्तुतश्च यास्त्वा वर्धन्ति महे राधसे नृम्णाय । इन्द्र कारिणं वृधन्तः ॥
8.2.e: And lauds which strengthen thee for great bounty and valour, and exalt  Indra who doeth glorious deeds,

8.2.d: गिरश्च यास्ते गिर्वाह उक्था च तुभ्यं तानि । सत्रा दधिरे शवांसि ॥
8.2.e: And songs to thee who lovest song, and all those hymns addressed to thee-  These evermore confirm thy might.

8.2.d: एवेदेष तुविकूर्मिर्वाजाँ एको वज्रहस्तः । सनादमृक्तो दयते ॥
8.2.e: Thus he, sole doer of great deeds whose hand holds thunder, gives us strength,  He who hath never been subdued.

8.2.d: हन्ता वृत्रं दक्षिणेनेन्द्रः पुरू पुरुहूतः । महान्महीभिः शचीभिः ॥
8.2.e: Vṛtra he slays with his right hand, even Indra, great with mighty power,  And much-invoked in many a place.

8.2.d: यस्मिन्विश्वाश्चर्षणय उत च्यौत्ना ज्रयांसि च । अनु घेन्मन्दी मघोनः ॥
8.2.e: He upon whom all men depend, all regions, all achievements, he  Takes pleasure in our wealthy chiefs.

8.2.d: एष एतानि चकारेन्द्रो विश्वा योऽति शृण्वे । वाजदावा मघोनाम् ॥
8.2.e: All this hath he accomplished, yea, Indra, most gloriously renowned,  Who gives our wealthy princes strength.

8.2.d: प्रभर्ता रथं गव्यन्तमपाकाच्चिद्यमवति । इनो वसु स हि वोळ्हा ॥
8.2.e: Who drives his chariot seeking spoil, from afar, to him he loves:  For swift is he to bring men wealth.

8.2.d: सनिता विप्रो अर्वद्भिर्हन्ता वृत्रं नृभिः शूरः । सत्योऽविता विधन्तम् ॥
8.2.e: The Sage who, winning spoil with steeds, slays Vṛtra, Hero with the men,  His servant's faithful succourer.

8.2.d: यजध्वैनं प्रियमेधा इन्द्रं सत्राचा मनसा । यो भूत्सोमैः सत्यमद्वा ॥
8.2.e: O Priyamedhas, worship with collected mind this Indra whom  The Soma hath full well inspired.

8.2.d: गाथश्रवसं सत्पतिं श्रवस्कामं पुरुत्मानम् । कण्वासो गात वाजिनम् ॥
8.2.e: Ye Kaṇvas, sing the Mighty One, Lord of the Brave, who loves renown,  All-present, glorified by song.

8.2.d: य ऋते चिद्गास्पदेभ्यो दात्सखा नृभ्यः शचीवान् । ये अस्मिन्काममश्रियन् ॥
8.2.e: Strong Friend, who, with no trace of feet, restores the cattle to the men,  Who rest their wish and hope on him.

8.2.d: इत्था धीवन्तमद्रिवः काण्वं मेध्यातिथिम् । मेषो भूतो३ऽभि यन्नयः ॥
8.2.e: Shaped as a Ram, Stone-hurler I once thou camest hither to the son  Of Kaṇva, wise Medhyātithi.

8.2.d: शिक्षा विभिन्दो अस्मै चत्वार्ययुता ददत् । अष्टा परः सहस्रा ॥
8.2.e: Vibhindu, thou hast helped this man, giving him thousands four times ten,  And afterward eight thousand more.

8.2.d: उत सु त्ये पयोवृधा माकी रणस्य नप्त्या । जनित्वनाय मामहे ॥
8.2.e: And these twain pouring streams of milk, creative, daughters of delight,  For wedlock sake I glorify.

8.3.d: पिबा सुतस्य रसिनो मत्स्वा न इन्द्र गोमतः । आपिर्नो बोधि सधमाद्यो वृधे३ऽस्माँ अवन्तु ते धियः ॥
8.3.e: DRINK, Indra, of the savoury juice, and cheer thee with our milky draught.  Be, for our weal, our Friend and sharer of the feast, and let thy wisdom guard us well.

8.3.d: भूयाम ते सुमतौ वाजिनो वयं मा नः स्तरभिमातये । अस्माञ्चित्राभिरवतादभिष्टिभिरा नः सुम्नेषु यामय ॥
8.3.e: In thy kind grace and favour may we still be strong: expose us not to foe's attack.  With manifold assistance guard and succour us, and bring us to felicity.

8.3.d: इमा उ त्वा पुरूवसो गिरो वर्धन्तु या मम । पावकवर्णाः शुचयो विपश्चितोऽभि स्तोमैरनूषत ॥
8.3.e: May these my songs of praise exalt thee, Lord, who hast abundant wealth.  Men skilled in holy hymns, pure, with the hues of fire, have sung them with their lauds to thee.

8.3.d: अयं सहस्रमृषिभिः सहस्कृतः समुद्र इव पप्रथे । सत्यः सो अस्य महिमा गृणे शवो यज्ञेषु विप्रराज्ये ॥
8.3.e: He, with his might enhanced by Ṛṣis thousandfold, hath like an ocean spread himself.  His majesty is praised as true at solemn rites, his power where holy singers rule.

8.3.d: इन्द्रमिद्देवतातय इन्द्रं प्रयत्यध्वरे । इन्द्रं समीके वनिनो हवामह इन्द्रं धनस्य सातये ॥
8.3.e: Indra for worship of the Gods, Indra while sacrifice proceeds,  Indra, as worshippers in battle-shock, we call, Indra that we may win the spoil.

8.3.d: इन्द्रो मह्ना रोदसी पप्रथच्छव इन्द्रः सूर्यमरोचयत् । इन्द्रे ह विश्वा भुवनानि येमिर इन्द्रे सुवानास इन्दवः ॥
8.3.e: With might hath Indra spread out heaven and earth, with power hath Indra lighted up the Sun.  In Indra are all creatures closely held; in him meet the distilling Soma-drops.

8.3.d: अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतय इन्द्र स्तोमेभिरायवः । समीचीनास ऋभवः समस्वरन्रुद्रा गृणन्त पूर्व्यम् ॥
8.3.e: Men with their lauds are urging thee, Indra, to drink the Soma first.  The Ṛbhus in accord have lifted up their voice, and Rudras sung thee as the first.

8.3.d: अस्येदिन्द्रो वावृधे वृष्ण्यं शवो मदे सुतस्य विष्णवि । अद्या तमस्य महिमानमायवोऽनु ष्टुवन्ति पूर्वथा ॥
8.3.e: Indra increased his manly strength at sacrifice, in the wild rapture of this juice.  And living men to-day, even as of old, sing forth their praises to his majesty.

8.3.d: तत्त्वा यामि सुवीर्यं तद्ब्रह्म पूर्वचित्तये । येना यतिभ्यो भृगवे धने हिते येन प्रस्कण्वमाविथ ॥
8.3.e: I crave of thee that hero strength, that thou mayst first regard this prayer,  Wherewith thou holpest Bhṛgu and the Yatis and Praskaṇva when the prize was staked.

8.3.d: येना समुद्रमसृजो महीरपस्तदिन्द्र वृष्णि ते शवः । सद्यः सो अस्य महिमा न संनशे यं क्षोणीरनुचक्रदे ॥
8.3.e: Wherewith thou sentest mighty waters to the sea, that, Indra, is thy manly strength.  For ever unattainable is this power of him to whom the worlds have cried aloud.

8.3.d: शग्धी न इन्द्र यत्त्वा रयिं यामि सुवीर्यम् । शग्धि वाजाय प्रथमं सिषासते शग्धि स्तोमाय पूर्व्य ॥
8.3.e: Help us, O Indra, when we pray to thee for wealth and hero might.  First help thou on to strength the man who strives to win, and aid our laud, O Ancient One.

8.3.d: शग्धी नो अस्य यद्ध पौरमाविथ धिय इन्द्र सिषासतः । शग्धि यथा रुशमं श्यावकं कृपमिन्द्र प्रावः स्वर्णरम् ॥
8.3.e: Help for us, Indra, as thou holpest Paura once, this man's devotions bent on gain.  Help, as thou gavest Ruśama and Śyāvaka and Svarṇara and Kṛpa aid.

8.3.d: कन्नव्यो अतसीनां तुरो गृणीत मर्त्यः । नही न्वस्य महिमानमिन्द्रियं स्वर्गृणन्त आनशुः ॥
8.3.e: What newest of imploring prayers shall, then, the zealous mortal sing?  For have not they who laud his might, and Indra-power won for themselves the light of heaven?

8.3.d: कदु स्तुवन्त ऋतयन्त देवत ऋषिः को विप्र ओहते । कदा हवं मघवन्निन्द्र सुन्वतः कदु स्तुवत आ गमः ॥
8.3.e: When shall they keep the Law and praise thee mid the Gods? Who counts as Ṛṣi and as sage?  When ever wilt thou, Indra Maghavan, come nigh to presser's or to praiser's call?

8.3.d: उदु त्ये मधुमत्तमा गिरः स्तोमास ईरते । सत्राजितो धनसा अक्षितोतयो वाजयन्तो रथा इव ॥
8.3.e: These songs of ours exceeding sweet, these hymns of praise ascend to thee,  Like ever-conquering chariots that display their strength, gain wealth, and give unfailing aid.

8.3.d: कण्वा इव भृगवः सूर्या इव विश्वमिद्धीतमानशुः । इन्द्रं स्तोमेभिर्महयन्त आयवः प्रियमेधासो अस्वरन् ॥
8.3.e: The Bhṛgus are like Suns, like Kaṇvas, and have gained all that their thoughts were bent upon.  The living men of Priyamedha's race have sung exalting Indra with their lauds.

8.3.d: युक्ष्वा हि वृत्रहन्तम हरी इन्द्र परावतः । अर्वाचीनो मघवन्त्सोमपीतय उग्र ऋष्वेभिरा गहि ॥
8.3.e: Best slayer of the Vṛtras, yoke thy Bay Steeds, Indra, from afar.  Come with the High Ones hither, Maghavan, to us, Mighty, to drink the Soma juice.

8.3.d: इमे हि ते कारवो वावशुर्धिया विप्रासो मेधसातये । स त्वं नो मघवन्निन्द्र गिर्वणो वेनो न शृणुधी हवम् ॥
8.3.e: For these, the bards and singers, have cried out to thee with prayer, to gain the sacrifice.  As such, O Maghavan, Indra, who lovest song, even as a lover bear my call.

8.3.d: निरिन्द्र बृहतीभ्यो वृत्रं धनुभ्यो अस्फुरः । निरर्बुदस्य मृगयस्य मायिनो निः पर्वतस्य गा आजः ॥
8.3.e: Thou from the lofty plains above, O Indra, hurledst Vṛtra down.  Thou dravest forth the kine of guileful Mṛgaya and Arbuda from the mountain's hold.

8.3.d: निरग्नयो रुरुचुर्निरु सूर्यो निः सोम इन्द्रियो रसः । निरन्तरिक्षादधमो महामहिं कृषे तदिन्द्र पौंस्यम् ॥
8.3.e: Bright were the flaming fires, the Sun gave forth his shine, and Soma, Indra's juice, shone clear.  Indra, thou blewest the great Dragon from the air: men must regard that valorous deed.

8.3.d: यं मे दुरिन्द्रो मरुतः पाकस्थामा कौरयाणः । विश्वेषां त्मना शोभिष्ठमुपेव दिवि धावमानम् ॥
8.3.e: The fairest courser of them all, who runneth on as ’twere to heaven.  Which Indra and the Maruts gave, and Pākasthāman Kaurayāṇ.

8.3.d: रोहितं मे पाकस्थामा सुधुरं कक्ष्यप्राम् । अदाद्रायो विबोधनम् ॥
8.3.e: To me hath Pākasthāman given, a ruddy horse, good at the pole,  Filling is girth and rousing wealth;

8.3.d: यस्मा अन्ये दश प्रति धुरं वहन्ति वह्नयः । अस्तं वयो न तुग्र्यम् ॥
8.3.e: Compared with whom no other ten strong coursers, harnessed to the pole,  Bear Tugrya to his dwelling place.

8.3.d: आत्मा पितुस्तनूर्वास ओजोदा अभ्यञ्जनम् । तुरीयमिद्रोहितस्य पाकस्थामानं भोजं दातारमब्रवम् ॥
8.3.e: Raiment is body, food is life, and healing ointment giveth strength.  As the free-handed giver of the ruddy steed, I have named Pākasthāman fourth.

8.4.d: यदिन्द्र प्रागपागुदङ्न्यग्वा हूयसे नृभिः । सिमा पुरू नृषूतो अस्यानवेऽसि प्रशर्ध तुर्वशे ॥
8.4.e: THOUGH, Indra, thou art called by men eastward and westward, north and south,  Thou chiefly art with Ānava and Turvaśa, brave Champion I urged by men to Come.

8.4.d: यद्वा रुमे रुशमे श्यावके कृप इन्द्र मादयसे सचा । कण्वासस्त्वा ब्रह्मभिः स्तोमवाहस इन्द्रा यच्छन्त्या गहि ॥
8.4.e: Or, Indra, when with Ruma, Ruśama, Śyāvaka, and Kṛpa thou rejoicest thee,  Still do the Kaṇvas, bringing praises, with their prayers, O Indra, draw thee hither: come.

8.4.d: यथा गौरो अपा कृतं तृष्यन्नेत्यवेरिणम् । आपित्वे नः प्रपित्वे तूयमा गहि कण्वेषु सु सचा पिब ॥
8.4.e: Even as the wild-bull, when he thirsts, goes to the desert's watery pool,  Come hither quickly both at morning and at eve, and with the Kaṇvas drink thy fill.

8.4.d: मन्दन्तु त्वा मघवन्निन्द्रेन्दवो राधोदेयाय सुन्वते । आमुष्या सोममपिबश्चमू सुतं ज्येष्ठं तद्दधिषे सहः ॥
8.4.e: May the drops gladden thee, rich Indra, and obtain bounty for him who pours the juice.  Soma pressed in the mortar didst thou take and drink, and hence hast won surpassing might.

8.4.d: प्र चक्रे सहसा सहो बभञ्ज मन्युमोजसा । विश्वे त इन्द्र पृतनायवो यहो नि वृक्षा इव येमिरे ॥
8.4.e: With mightier strength he conquered strength, with energy he crushed their wrath.  O Indra, Strong in youth, all those who sought the fray bent and bowed down to thee like trees.

8.4.d: सहस्रेणेव सचते यवीयुधा यस्त आनळुपस्तुतिम् । पुत्रं प्रावर्गं कृणुते सुवीर्ये दाश्नोति नमउक्तिभिः ॥
8.4.e: He who wins promise of thine aid goes girt as with a thousand mighty men of war.  He makes his son preeminent in hero might: he serves with reverential prayer.

8.4.d: मा भेम मा श्रमिष्मोग्रस्य सख्ये तव । महत्ते वृष्णो अभिचक्ष्यं कृतं पश्येम तुर्वशं यदुम् ॥
8.4.e: With thee, the Mighty, for our Friend, we will not fear or feel fatigue.  May we see Turvaśa and Yadu: thy great deed, O Hero, must be glorified.

8.4.d: सव्यामनु स्फिग्यं वावसे वृषा न दानो अस्य रोषति । मध्वा सम्पृक्ताः सारघेण धेनवस्तूयमेहि द्रवा पिब ॥
8.4.e: On his left hip the Hero hath reclined himself: the proffered feast offends him not.  The milk is blended with the honey of the bee: quickly come hither, baste, and drink.

8.4.d: अश्वी रथी सुरूप इद्गोमाँ इदिन्द्र ते सखा । श्वात्रभाजा वयसा सचते सदा चन्द्रो याति सभामुप ॥
8.4.e: Indra, thy friend is fair of form and rich in horses, cars, and kine.  He evermore hath food accompanied by wealth, and radiant joins the company.

8.4.d: ऋश्यो न तृष्यन्नवपानमा गहि पिबा सोमं वशाँ अनु । निमेघमानो मघवन्दिवेदिव ओजिष्ठं दधिषे सहः ॥
8.4.e: Come like a thirsty antelope to the drinking-place: drink Soma to thy heart's desire.  Raining it down, O Maghavan, day after day, thou gainest thy surpassing might.

8.4.d: अध्वर्यो द्रावया त्वं सोममिन्द्रः पिपासति । उप नूनं युयुजे वृषणा हरी आ च जगाम वृत्रहा ॥
8.4.e: Priest, let the Soma juice flow forth, for Indra longs to drink thereof.  He even now hath yoked his vigorous Bay Steeds: the Vṛtra-slayer hath come near.

8.4.d: स्वयं चित्स मन्यते दाशुरिर्जनो यत्रा सोमस्य तृम्पसि । इदं ते अन्नं युज्यं समुक्षितं तस्येहि प्र द्रवा पिब ॥
8.4.e: The man with whom thou fillcst thee with Soma deems himself a pious worshipper.  This thine appropriate food is here poured out for thee: come, hasten forward. drink of it,

8.4.d: रथेष्ठायाध्वर्यवः सोममिन्द्राय सोतन । अधि ब्रध्नस्याद्रयो वि चक्षते सुन्वन्तो दाश्वध्वरम् ॥
8.4.e: Press out the Soma juice, ye priests, for Indra borne upon his car.  The pressing-stones speak loud of Indra, while they shed the juice which, offered, honours him.

8.4.d: उप ब्रध्नं वावाता वृषणा हरी इन्द्रमपसु वक्षतः । अर्वाञ्चं त्वा सप्तयोऽध्वरश्रियो वहन्तु सवनेदुप ॥
8.4.e: To the brown juice may his dear vigorous Bay Steeds bring Indra, to our holy task.  Hither let thy Car-steeds who seek the sacrifice bring thee to our drink-offerings.

8.4.d: प्र पूषणं वृणीमहे युज्याय पुरूवसुम् । स शक्र शिक्ष पुरुहूत नो धिया तुजे राये विमोचन ॥
8.4.e: Pūṣan, the Lord of ample wealth, for firm alliance we elect.  May he with wisdom, Śakra! Looser! Much-invoked! aid us to riches and to seed.

8.4.d: सं नः शिशीहि भुरिजोरिव क्षुरं रास्व रायो विमोचन । त्वे तन्नः सुवेदमुस्रियं वसु यं त्वं हिनोषि मर्त्यम् ॥
8.4.e: Sharpen us like a razor in the barber's hands: send riches thou who settest free.  Easy to find with thee are treasures of the Dawn for mortal man whom thou dost speed.

8.4.d: वेमि त्वा पूषन्नृञ्जसे वेमि स्तोतव आघृणे । न तस्य वेम्यरणं हि तद्वसो स्तुषे पज्राय साम्ने ॥
8.4.e: Pūṣan, I long to win thy love, I long to praise thee, Radiant God.  Excellent Lord, ’tis strange tome, no wish have I to sing the psalm that Pajra sings.

8.4.d: परा गावो यवसं कच्चिदाघृणे नित्यं रेक्णो अमर्त्य । अस्माकं पूषन्नविता शिवो भव मंहिष्ठो वाजसातये ॥
8.4.e: My kine, O Radiant God, seek pasture where they will, my during wealth, Immortal One.  Be our protector, Pūṣan! be, most liberal Lord, propitious to our gathering strength.

8.4.d: स्थूरं राधः शताश्वं कुरुङ्गस्य दिविष्टिषु । राज्ञस्त्वेषस्य सुभगस्य रातिषु तुर्वशेष्वमन्महि ॥
8.4.e: Rich was the gift Kurunga gave, a hundred steeds at morning rites.  Among the gifts of Turvaśas we thought of him, the opulent, the splendid King.

8.4.d: धीभिः सातानि काण्वस्य वाजिनः प्रियमेधैरभिद्युभिः । षष्टिं सहस्रानु निर्मजामजे निर्यूथानि गवामृषिः ॥
8.4.e: What by his morning songs Kaṇva, the powerful, hath, with the Priyamedhas, gained-

8.4.d: वृक्षाश्चिन्मे अभिपित्वे अरारणुः । गां भजन्त मेहनाश्वं भजन्त मेहना ॥
8.4.e: The very trees were joyful at my coming: kine they obtained in plenty, steeds in plenty.

8.5.d: दूरादिहेव यत्सत्यरुणप्सुरशिश्वितत् । वि भानुं विश्वधातनत् ॥
8.5.e: WHEN, even as she were present here, red Dawn hath shone from far away,  She spreadeth light on every side.

8.5.d: नृवद्दस्रा मनोयुजा रथेन पृथुपाजसा । सचेथे अश्विनोषसम् ॥
8.5.e: Like Heroes on your will-yoked car farshining, Wonder-Workers! ye  Attend, O Aśvins, on the Dawn.

8.5.d: युवाभ्यां वाजिनीवसू प्रति स्तोमा अदृक्षत । वाचं दूतो यथोहिषे ॥
8.5.e: By you, O Lords of ample wealth our songs of praise have been observed:  As envoy have I brought the prayer.

8.5.d: पुरुप्रिया ण ऊतये पुरुमन्द्रा पुरूवसू । स्तुषे कण्वासो अश्विना ॥
8.5.e: Kaṇvas must praise the Aśvins dear to many, making many glad,  Most rich, that they may succour us.

8.5.d: मंहिष्ठा वाजसातमेषयन्ता शुभस्पती । गन्तारा दाशुषो गृहम् ॥
8.5.e: Most liberal, best at winning strength, inciters, Lords of splendour who  Visit the worshipper's abode.

8.5.d: ता सुदेवाय दाशुषे सुमेधामवितारिणीम् । घृतैर्गव्यूतिमुक्षतम् ॥
8.5.e: So for devout Sudeva dew with fatness his unfailing mead,  And make it rich for sacrifice.

8.5.d: आ नः स्तोममुप द्रवत्तूयं श्येनेभिराशुभिः । यातमश्वेभिरश्विना ॥
8.5.e: Hitherward running speedily with horses, as with rapid hawks,  Come, Aśvins, to our song of praise

8.5.d: येभिस्तिस्रः परावतो दिवो विश्वानि रोचना । त्रीँरक्तून्परिदीयथः ॥
8.5.e: Wherewith the three wide distances, and all the lights that are in heaven.  Ye traverse, and three times of night.

8.5.d: उत नो गोमतीरिष उत सातीरहर्विदा । वि पथः सातये सितम् ॥
8.5.e: O Finders of the Day, that we may win us food of kine and wealth,  Open the paths for us to tread.

8.5.d: आ नो गोमन्तमश्विना सुवीरं सुरथं रयिम् । वोळ्हमश्वावतीरिषः ॥
8.5.e: O Aśvins, bring us wealth in kine, in noble heroes, and in cars:  Bring us the strength that horses give.

8.5.d: वावृधाना शुभस्पती दस्रा हिरण्यवर्तनी । पिबतं सोम्यं मधु ॥
8.5.e: Ye Lords of splendour, glorified, ye Wonder-Workers borne on paths  Of gold, drink sweets with Somajuice.

8.5.d: अस्मभ्यं वाजिनीवसू मघवद्भ्यश्च सप्रथः । छर्दिर्यन्तमदाभ्यम् ॥
8.5.e: To us, ye Lords of ample wealth, and to our wealth chiefs extend  Wide shelter, ne’er to be assailed.

8.5.d: नि षु ब्रह्म जनानां याविष्टं तूयमा गतम् । मो ष्व१न्याँ उपारतम् ॥
8.5.e: Come quickly downward to the prayer of people whom ye favour most:  Approach not unto other folk.

8.5.d: अस्य पिबतमश्विना युवं मदस्य चारुणः । मध्वो रातस्य धिष्ण्या ॥
8.5.e: Ye Aśvins whom our minds perceive, drink of this lovely gladdening draught,  The mcath which we present to you.

8.5.d: अस्मे आ वहतं रयिं शतवन्तं सहस्रिणम् । पुरुक्षुं विश्वधायसम् ॥
8.5.e: Bring riches hither unto us in hundreds and in thousands, source  Of plenteous food, sustaining all.

8.5.d: पुरुत्रा चिद्धि वां नरा विह्वयन्ते मनीषिणः । वाघद्भिरश्विना गतम् ॥
8.5.e: Verily sages call on you, ye Heroes, in full many a place.  Moved by the priests, O Aśvins, conic.

8.5.d: जनासो वृक्तबर्हिषो हविष्मन्तो अरंकृतः । युवां हवन्ते अश्विना ॥
8.5.e: Men who have trimmed the sacred grass, bringing oblations and prepared,  O Aśvins, are invoking you.

8.5.d: अस्माकमद्य वामयं स्तोमो वाहिष्ठो अन्तमः । युवाभ्यां भूत्वश्विना ॥
8.5.e: May this our hymn of praise to-day, most powerful to bring you, be,  O Aśvins, nearest to your hearts.

8.5.d: यो ह वां मधुनो दृतिराहितो रथचर्षणे । ततः पिबतमश्विना ॥
8.5.e: The skin filled full of savoury meath, laid in the pathway of your car-  O Aśvins, drink ye both therefrom.

8.5.d: तेन नो वाजिनीवसू पश्वे तोकाय शं गवे । वहतं पीवरीरिषः ॥
8.5.e: For this, ye Lords of ample wealth, bring blessing for our herd, our kine,  Our progeny, and plenteous food.

8.5.d: उत नो दिव्या इष उत सिन्धूँरहर्विदा । अप द्वारेव वर्षथः ॥
8.5.e: Ye too unclose to us like doors the strengthening waters of the sky,  And rivers, ye who find the day.

8.5.d: कदा वां तौग्र्यो विधत्समुद्रे जहितो नरा । यद्वां रथो विभिष्पतात् ॥
8.5.e: When did the son of Tugra serve you, Men? Abandoned in the sea,  That with winged steeds your car might fly.

8.5.d: युवं कण्वाय नासत्या ऋपिरिप्ताय हर्म्ये । शश्वदूतीर्दशस्यथः ॥
8.5.e: Ye, O Nāsatyas, ministered to Kaṇva with repeated aid,  When cast into the heated pit.

8.5.d: ताभिरा यातमूतिभिर्नव्यसीभिः सुशस्तिभिः । यद्वां वृषण्वसू हुवे ॥
8.5.e: Come near with those most recent aids of yours which merit eulogy,  When I invoke you, Wealthy Gods.

8.5.d: यथा चित्कण्वमावतं प्रियमेधमुपस्तुतम् । अत्रिं शिञ्जारमश्विना ॥
8.5.e: As ye protected Kaṇva erst, Priyamedha and Upastuta,  Atri, Sinjara, Aśvins Twain

8.5.d: यथोत कृत्व्ये धनेंऽशुं गोष्वगस्त्यम् । यथा वाजेषु सोभरिम् ॥
8.5.e: And Amsu in decisive fight, Agastya in the fray for kine.  And, in his battles, Sobhari.

8.5.d: एतावद्वां वृषण्वसू अतो वा भूयो अश्विना । गृणन्तः सुम्नमीमहे ॥
8.5.e: For so much bliss, or even more, O Aśvins, Wealthy Gods, than this,  We pray white singing hymns to you.

8.5.d: रथं हिरण्यवन्धुरं हिरण्याभीशुमश्विना । आ हि स्थाथो दिविस्पृशम् ॥
8.5.e: Ascend your car with golden seat, O Aśvins, and with reins of gold,  That reaches even to the sky.

8.5.d: हिरण्ययी वां रभिरीषा अक्षो हिरण्ययः । उभा चक्रा हिरण्यया ॥
8.5.e: Golden is its supporting shaft, the axle also is of gold,  And both the wheels are made of gold.

8.5.d: तेन नो वाजिनीवसू परावतश्चिदा गतम् । उपेमां सुष्टुतिं मम ॥
8.5.e: Thereon, ye Lords of ample wealth, come to us even from afar,  Come ye to this mine eulogy.

8.5.d: आ वहेथे पराकात्पूर्वीरश्नन्तावश्विना । इषो दासीरमर्त्या ॥
8.5.e: From far away ye come to us, Aśvins, enjoying plenteous food  Of Dāsas, O Immortal Ones.

8.5.d: आ नो द्युम्नैरा श्रवोभिरा राया यातमश्विना । पुरुश्चन्द्रा नासत्या ॥
8.5.e: With splendour, riches, and renown, O Aśvins, hither come to us,  Nāsatyas, shining brilliantly.

8.5.d: एह वां प्रुषितप्सवो वयो वहन्तु पर्णिनः । अच्छा स्वध्वरं जनम् ॥
8.5.e: May dappled horses, steeds who fly with pinions, bring you hitherward  To people skilled in sacrifice.

8.5.d: रथं वामनुगायसं य इषा वर्तते सह । न चक्रमभि बाधते ॥
8.5.e: The whcel delayeth not that car of yours accompanied by song,  That cometh with a store of food.

8.5.d: हिरण्ययेन रथेन द्रवत्पाणिभिरश्वैः । धीजवना नासत्या ॥
8.5.e: Borne on that chariot wrought of gold, with coursers very fleet of foot,  Come, O Nāsatyas, swift as thought.

8.5.d: युवं मृगं जागृवांसं स्वदथो वा वृषण्वसू । ता नः पृङ्क्तमिषा रयिम् ॥
8.5.e: O Wealthy Gods, ye taste and find the brisk and watchful wild beast good.  Associate wealth with food for us.

8.5.d: ता मे अश्विना सनीनां विद्यातं नवानाम् । यथा चिच्चैद्यः कशुः शतमुष्ट्रानां ददत्सहस्रा दश गोनाम् ॥
8.5.e: As such, O Aśvins, find for me my share of new-presented gifts,  As Kasu, Cedi's son, gave me a hundred head of buffaloes, and ten thousand kine.

8.5.d: यो मे हिरण्यसंदृशो दश राज्ञो अमंहत । अधस्पदा इच्चैद्यस्य कृष्टयश्चर्मम्ना अभितो जनाः ॥
8.5.e: He who hath given me for mine own ten Kings like gold to look upon.  At Caidya's feet are all the people round about, all those who think upon the shield.

8.5.d: माकिरेना पथा गाद्येनेमे यन्ति चेदयः । अन्यो नेत्सूरिरोहते भूरिदावत्तरो जनः ॥
8.5.e: No man, not any, goes upon the path on which the Cedis walk.  No other prince, no folk is held more liberal of gifts than they.

8.6.d: महाँ इन्द्रो य ओजसा पर्जन्यो वृष्टिमाँ इव । स्तोमैर्वत्सस्य वावृधे ॥
8.6.e: INDRA, great in his power and might, and like Parjanya rich in rain,  Is magnified by Vatsa's lauds.

8.6.d: प्रजामृतस्य पिप्रतः प्र यद्भरन्त वह्नयः । विप्रा ऋतस्य वाहसा ॥
8.6.e: When the priests, strengthening the Son of Holy Law, present their gifts,  Singers with Order's hymn of praiser.

8.6.d: कण्वा इन्द्रं यदक्रत स्तोमैर्यज्ञस्य साधनम् । जामि ब्रुवत आयुधम् ॥
8.6.e: Since Kaṇvas with their lauds have made Indra complete the sacrifice.  Words are their own appropriate arms.

8.6.d: समस्य मन्यवे विशो विश्वा नमन्त कृष्टयः । समुद्रायेव सिन्धवः ॥
8.6.e: Before his hot displeasure all the peoples, all the men, bow down,  As rivers bow them to the sea.

8.6.d: ओजस्तदस्य तित्विष उभे यत्समवर्तयत् । इन्द्रश्चर्मेव रोदसी ॥
8.6.e: This power of his shone brightly forth when Indra brought together, like  A skin, the worlds of heaven and earth.

8.6.d: वि चिद्वृत्रस्य दोधतो वज्रेण शतपर्वणा । शिरो बिभेद वृष्णिना ॥
8.6.e: The fiercely-moving Vṛtra's head he severed with his thunderbolt,  His mighty hundred-knotted bolt.

8.6.d: इमा अभि प्र णोनुमो विपामग्रेषु धीतयः । अग्नेः शोचिर्न दिद्युतः ॥
8.6.e: Here are-we sing them loudly forth-our thoughts among-the best of songs.  Even lightnings like the blaze of fire.

8.6.d: गुहा सतीरुप त्मना प्र यच्छोचन्त धीतयः । कण्वा ऋतस्य धारया ॥
8.6.e: When bidden thoughts, spontaneously advancing, glow, and with the stream  Of sacrifice the Kaṇvas shine.

8.6.d: प्र तमिन्द्र नशीमहि रयिं गोमन्तमश्विनम् । प्र ब्रह्म पूर्वचित्तये ॥
8.6.e: Indra, may we obtain that wealth in horses and in herds of cows,  And prayer that may be noticed first.

8.6.d: अहमिद्धि पितुष्परि मेधामृतस्य जग्रभ । अहं सूर्य इवाजनि ॥
8.6.e: I from my Father have received deep knowledge of the Holy Law  I was born like unto the Sun.

8.6.d: अहं प्रत्नेन मन्मना गिरः शुम्भामि कण्ववत् । येनेन्द्रः शुष्ममिद्दधे ॥
8.6.e: After the lore of ancient time I make, like Kaṇva, beauteous songs,  And Indra's selfgains strength thereby.

8.6.d: ये त्वामिन्द्र न तुष्टुवुर्ऋषयो ये च तुष्टुवुः । ममेद्वर्धस्व सुष्टुतः ॥
8.6.e: Whatever Ṛṣis have not praised thee, Indra, or have lauded thee,  By me exalted wax thou strong.

8.6.d: यदस्य मन्युरध्वनीद्वि वृत्रं पर्वशो रुजन् । अपः समुद्रमैरयत् ॥
8.6.e: When his wrath thundered, when he rent Vṛtra to pieces, limb by limb,  He sent the waters to the sea.

8.6.d: नि शुष्ण इन्द्र धर्णसिं वज्रं जघन्थ दस्यवि । वृषा ह्युग्र शृण्विषे ॥
8.6.e: Against the Dasyu gusna thou, Indra, didst hurl thy during bolt:  Thou, Dread one, hast a hero's fame.

8.6.d: न द्याव इन्द्रमोजसा नान्तरिक्षाणि वज्रिणम् । न विव्यचन्त भूमयः ॥
8.6.e: Neither the heavens nor firmaments nor regions of the earth contain  Indra, the Thunderer with his might.

8.6.d: यस्त इन्द्र महीरपः स्तभूयमान आशयत् । नि तं पद्यासु शिश्नथः ॥
8.6.e: O Indra him who lay at length staying thy copious waters thou,  In his own footsteps, smotest down

8.6.d: य इमे रोदसी मही समीची समजग्रभीत् । तमोभिरिन्द्र तं गुहः ॥
8.6.e: Thou hiddest deep in darkness itim, O Indra, who had set his grasp  On spacious heaven and earth conjoined.

8.6.d: य इन्द्र यतयस्त्वा भृगवो ये च तुष्टुवुः । ममेदुग्र श्रुधी हवम् ॥
8.6.e: Indra, whatever Yatis and Bhṛgus have offered praise to thee,  Listen, thou Mighty, to my call.

8.6.d: इमास्त इन्द्र पृश्नयो घृतं दुहत आशिरम् । एनामृतस्य पिप्युषीः ॥
8.6.e: Indra, these spotted cows yield thee their butter and the milky draught;  Aiders, thereby, of sacrifice;

8.6.d: या इन्द्र प्रस्वस्त्वासा गर्भमचक्रिरन् । परि धर्मेव सूर्यम् ॥
8.6.e: Which, teeming, have received thee as a life-germ, Indra, with their mouth,  Like Sūrya who sustaineth all.

8.6.d: त्वामिच्छवसस्पते कण्वा उक्थेन वावृधुः । त्वां सुतास इन्दवः ॥
8.6.e: O Lord of Might, with hymns of praise the Kaṇvas have increased thy power,  The drops poured forth have strengthened thee.

8.6.d: तवेदिन्द्र प्रणीतिषूत प्रशस्तिरद्रिवः । यज्ञो वितन्तसाय्यः ॥
8.6.e: Under thy guidance, Indra, mid thy praises, Lord of Thunder, shall  The sacrifice be soon performed.

8.6.d: आ न इन्द्र महीमिषं पुरं न दर्षि गोमतीम् । उत प्रजां सुवीर्यम् ॥
8.6.e: Indra, disclose much food for us, like a stronghold with store of kine:  Give progeny and heroic strength.

8.6.d: उत त्यदाश्वश्व्यं यदिन्द्र नाहुषीष्वा । अग्रे विक्षु प्रदीदयत् ॥
8.6.e: And, Indra, grant us all that wealth of fleet steeds which shone bright of old  Among the tribes of Nahusas.

8.6.d: अभि व्रजं न तत्निषे सूर उपाकचक्षसम् । यदिन्द्र मृळयासि नः ॥
8.6.e: Hither thou seemest to attract heaven's fold which shines before our eyes,  When, Indra, thou art kind to us.

8.6.d: यदङ्ग तविषीयस इन्द्र प्रराजसि क्षितीः । महाँ अपार ओजसा ॥
8.6.e: Yea, when thou puttest forth thy power, Indra, thou governest the folk.  Mighty, unlimited in strength.

8.6.d: तं त्वा हविष्मतीर्विश उप ब्रुवत ऊतये । उरुज्रयसमिन्दुभिः ॥
8.6.e: The tribes who bring oblations call to thee, to thee to give them help,  With drops to thee who spreadest far.

8.6.d: उपह्वरे गिरीणां संगथे च नदीनाम् । धिया विप्रो अजायत ॥
8.6.e: There where the mountains downward slope, there by the meeting of the streams  The Sage was manifest with song.

8.6.d: अतः समुद्रमुद्वतश्चिकित्वाँ अव पश्यति । यतो विपान एजति ॥
8.6.e: Thence, marking, from his lofty place downward he looks upon the sea,  And thence with rapid stir he moves.

8.6.d: आदित्प्रत्नस्य रेतसो ज्योतिष्पश्यन्ति वासरम् । परो यदिध्यते दिवा ॥
8.6.e: Then, verify, they see the light refulgent of primeval seed,  Kindled on yonder side of heaven.

8.6.d: कण्वास इन्द्र ते मतिं विश्वे वर्धन्ति पौंस्यम् । उतो शविष्ठ वृष्ण्यम् ॥
8.6.e: Indra, the Kaṇvas all exalt thy wisdom and thy manly power,  And, Mightiest! thine heroic strength.

8.6.d: इमां म इन्द्र सुष्टुतिं जुषस्व प्र सु मामव । उत प्र वर्धया मतिम् ॥
8.6.e: Accept this eulogy of mine, Indra, and guard me carefully:  Strengthen my thought and prosper it.

8.6.d: उत ब्रह्मण्या वयं तुभ्यं प्रवृद्ध वज्रिवः । विप्रा अतक्ष्म जीवसे ॥
8.6.e: For thee, O Mighty, Thunder-armed, we singers through devotionhave  Fashioned the hymn that we may live.

8.6.d: अभि कण्वा अनूषतापो न प्रवता यतीः । इन्द्रं वनन्वती मतिः ॥
8.6.e: To Indra have the Kaṇvas sung, like waters speeding down a slope:  The song is fain to go to him.

8.6.d: इन्द्रमुक्थानि वावृधुः समुद्रमिव सिन्धवः । अनुत्तमन्युमजरम् ॥
8.6.e: As rivers swell the ocean, so our hymns of praise make Indra strong,  Eternal, of resistIess wrath.

8.6.d: आ नो याहि परावतो हरिभ्यां हर्यताभ्याम् । इममिन्द्र सुतं पिब ॥
8.6.e: Come with thy lovely Bay Steeds, come to us from regions far away  O Indra, drink this Soma juice.

8.6.d: त्वामिद्वृत्रहन्तम जनासो वृक्तबर्हिषः । हवन्ते वाजसातये ॥
8.6.e: Best slayer of Vṛtras, men whose sacred grass is ready trimmed  Invoke thee for the gain of spoil.

8.6.d: अनु त्वा रोदसी उभे चक्रं न वर्त्येतशम् । अनु सुवानास इन्दवः ॥
8.6.e: The heavens and earth come after thee as the wheel follows Etaśa:  To thee flow Soma-drops effused.

8.6.d: मन्दस्वा सु स्वर्णर उतेन्द्र शर्यणावति । मत्स्वा विवस्वतो मती ॥
8.6.e: Rejoice, O Indra, in the light, rejoice in Saryandyan, be Glad in the sacrificer's hymn.

8.6.d: वावृधान उप द्यवि वृषा वज्र्यरोरवीत् । वृत्रहा सोमपातमः ॥
8.6.e: Grown strong in heaven, the Thunder-armed hath bellowed, Vṛtra-slayer, Bull,  Chief drinker of the Soma juice.

8.6.d: ऋषिर्हि पूर्वजा अस्येक ईशान ओजसा । इन्द्र चोष्कूयसे वसु ॥
8.6.e: Thou art a Ṛṣi born of old, sole Ruler over all by might:  Thou, Indra, guardest well our wealth.

8.6.d: अस्माकं त्वा सुताँ उप वीतपृष्ठा अभि प्रयः । शतं वहन्तु हरयः ॥
8.6.e: May thy Bay Steeds with beauteous backs, a hundred, bring thee to the feast,  Bring thee to these our Soma-draughts.

8.6.d: इमां सु पूर्व्यां धियं मधोर्घृतस्य पिप्युषीम् । कण्वा उक्थेन वावृधुः ॥
8.6.e: The Kaṇvas with their hymns of praise have magnified this ancient thought  That swells with streams of meath and oil.

8.6.d: इन्द्रमिद्विमहीनां मेधे वृणीत मर्त्यः । इन्द्रं सनिष्युरूतये ॥
8.6.e: Mid mightiest Gods let mortal man choose Indra at the sacrifice,  Indra, whoe’er would win, for help.

8.6.d: अर्वाञ्चं त्वा पुरुष्टुत प्रियमेधस्तुता हरी । सोमपेयाय वक्षतः ॥
8.6.e: Thy steeds, by Priyamedhas praised, shall bring thee, God whom all invoke,  Hither to drink the Somajuice.

8.6.d: शतमहं तिरिन्दिरे सहस्रं पर्शावा ददे । राधांसि याद्वानाम् ॥
8.6.e: A hundred thousand have I gained from Parsu, from Tirindira,  And presents of the Yadavas.

8.6.d: त्रीणि शतान्यर्वतां सहस्रा दश गोनाम् । ददुष्पज्राय साम्ने ॥
8.6.e: Ten thousand head of kine, and steeds three times a hundred they bestowed  On Pajra for the Sāma-song.

8.6.d: उदानट् ककुहो दिवमुष्ट्राञ्चतुर्युजो ददत् । श्रवसा याद्वं जनम् ॥
8.6.e: Kakuha hath reached up to heaven, bestowing buffaloes yoked in fours,  And matched in fame the Yadavas.

8.7.d: प्र यद्वस्त्रिष्टुभमिषं मरुतो विप्रो अक्षरत् । वि पर्वतेषु राजथ ॥
8.7.e: O MARUTS, when the sage hath poured the Tṛṣṭup forth as food for you,  Ye shine amid the mountain-clouds.

8.7.d: यदङ्ग तविषीयवो यामं शुभ्रा अचिध्वम् । नि पर्वता अहासत ॥
8.7.e: When, Bright Ones, fain to show your might ye have determined on your course,  The mountain-clouds have bent them down.

8.7.d: उदीरयन्त वायुभिर्वाश्रासः पृश्निमातरः । धुक्षन्त पिप्युषीमिषम् ॥
8.7.e: Loud roaring with the winds the Sons of Pṛśni have upraised themselves:  They have poured out the streaming food.

8.7.d: वपन्ति मरुतो मिहं प्र वेपयन्ति पर्वतान् । यद्यामं यान्ति वायुभिः ॥
8.7.e: The Maruts spread the mist abroad and make mountains rock and reel,  When with the winds they go their way

8.7.d: नि यद्यामाय वो गिरिर्नि सिन्धवो विधर्मणे । महे शुष्माय येमिरे ॥
8.7.e: What time the rivers and the hills before your coming bowed them down,  So to sustain your mighty force.

8.7.d: युष्माँ उ नक्तमूतये युष्मान्दिवा हवामहे । युष्मान्प्रयत्यध्वरे ॥
8.7.e: We call on you for aid by night, on you for succour in the day,  On you while sacrifice proceeds.

8.7.d: उदु त्ये अरुणप्सवश्चित्रा यामेभिरीरते । वाश्रा अधि ष्णुना दिवः ॥
8.7.e: These, verily, wondrous, red of hue, speed on their courses with a roar  Over the ridges of the sky.

8.7.d: सृजन्ति रश्मिमोजसा पन्थां सूर्याय यातवे । ते भानुभिर्वि तस्थिरे ॥
8.7.e: With might they drop the loosened rein so that the Sun may run his course,  And spread themselves with beams of light.

8.7.d: इमां मे मरुतो गिरमिमं स्तोममृभुक्षणः । इमं मे वनता हवम् ॥
8.7.e: Accept, ye Maruts, this my song, accept ye this mine hymn of praise,  Accept, Ṛbhukṣans, this my call.

8.7.d: त्रीणि सरांसि पृश्नयो दुदुह्रे वज्रिणे मधु । उत्सं कवन्धमुद्रिणम् ॥
8.7.e: The dappled Cows have poured three lakes, meath for the Thunder-wielding God,  From the great cask, the watery cloud.

8.7.d: मरुतो यद्ध वो दिवः सुम्नायन्तो हवामहे । आ तू न उप गन्तन ॥
8.7.e: O Maruts, quickly come to us when, longing for felicity,  We call you hither from the sky.

8.7.d: यूयं हि ष्ठा सुदानवो रुद्रा ऋभुक्षणो दमे । उत प्रचेतसो मदे ॥
8.7.e: For, Rudras and Ṛbhukṣans, ye, Most Bountiful, are in the house,  Wise when the gladdening draught is drunk.

8.7.d: आ नो रयिं मदच्युतं पुरुक्षुं विश्वधायसम् । इयर्ता मरुतो दिवः ॥
8.7.e: O Maruts, send us down from heaven riches distilling rapturous joy,  With plenteous food, sustaining all.

8.7.d: अधीव यद्गिरीणां यामं शुभ्रा अचिध्वम् । सुवानैर्मन्दध्व इन्दुभिः ॥
8.7.e: When, Bright Ones, hither from the hills ye have resolved to take your way,  Ye revel in the drops effused.

8.7.d: एतावतश्चिदेषां सुम्नं भिक्षेत मर्त्यः । अदाभ्यस्य मन्मभिः ॥
8.7.e: Man should solicit with his lauds happiness which belongs to them,  So great a band invincible.

8.7.d: ये द्रप्सा इव रोदसी धमन्त्यनु वृष्टिभिः । उत्सं दुहन्तो अक्षितम् ॥
8.7.e: They who like fiery sparks with showers of rain blow through the heaven and earth,  Milking the spring that never fails.

8.7.d: उदु स्वानेभिरीरत उद्रथैरुदु वायुभिः । उत्स्तोमैः पृश्निमातरः ॥
8.7.e: With chariots and tumultuous roar, with tempests and with hymns of praise  The Sons of Pṛśni hurry forth.

8.7.d: येनाव तुर्वशं यदुं येन कण्वं धनस्पृतम् । राये सु तस्य धीमहि ॥
8.7.e: For wealth, we think of that whereby ye aided Yadu, Turvaśa,  And KanVa who obtained the spoil.

8.7.d: इमा उ वः सुदानवो घृतं न पिप्युषीरिषः । वर्धान्काण्वस्य मन्मभिः ॥
8.7.e: May these our viands Bounteous Ones I that flow in streams like holy oil,  With Kaṇva's hymns, increase your might.

8.7.d: क्व नूनं सुदानवो मदथा वृक्तबर्हिषः । ब्रह्मा को वः सपर्यति ॥
8.7.e: Where, Bounteous Lords for whom the grass is trimmed, are ye rejoicing now?  What Brahman is adoring you?

8.7.d: नहि ष्म यद्ध वः पुरा स्तोमेभिर्वृक्तबर्हिषः । शर्धाँ ऋतस्य जिन्वथ ॥
8.7.e: Is it not there where ye of old, supplied with sacred grass, for lauds  Inspired the strong in sacrifice?

8.7.d: समु त्ये महतीरपः सं क्षोणी समु सूर्यम् । सं वज्रं पर्वशो दधुः ॥
8.7.e: They brought together both the worlds, the mighty waters, and the Sun,  And, joint by joint, the thunderbolt.

8.7.d: वि वृत्रं पर्वशो ययुर्वि पर्वताँ अराजिनः । चक्राणा वृष्णि पौंस्यम् ॥
8.7.e: They sundered Vṛtra limb from limb and split the gloomy mountain-clouds,  Performing a heroic deed.

8.7.d: अनु त्रितस्य युध्यतः शुष्ममावन्नुत क्रतुम् । अन्विन्द्रं वृत्रतूर्ये ॥
8.7.e: They reinforced the power and strength of Trita as he fought, and helped  Indra in battle with the foe.

8.7.d: विद्युद्धस्ता अभिद्यवः शिप्राः शीर्षन्हिरण्ययीः । शुभ्रा व्यञ्जत श्रिये ॥
8.7.e: They deck themselves for glory, bright, celestial, lightning in their hands,  And helms of gold upon their heads.

8.7.d: उशना यत्परावत उक्ष्णो रन्ध्रमयातन । द्यौर्न चक्रदद्भिया ॥
8.7.e: When eagerly ye from far away came to the cavern of the Bull,  He bellowed in his fear like Heaven.

8.7.d: आ नो मखस्य दावनेऽश्वैर्हिरण्यपाणिभिः । देवास उप गन्तन ॥
8.7.e: Borne by your golden-footed steeds, O Gods, come hither to receive  The sacrifice we offer you.

8.7.d: यदेषां पृषती रथे प्रष्टिर्वहति रोहितः । यान्ति शुभ्रा रिणन्नपः ॥
8.7.e: When the red leader draws along their spotted deer yoked to the car.  The Bright Ones come, and shed the rain.

8.7.d: सुषोमे शर्यणावत्यार्जीके पस्त्यावति । ययुर्निचक्रया नरः ॥
8.7.e: Susoma, Saryakiavan, and Arjika full of homes, have they.  These Heroes, sought with downward car.

8.7.d: कदा गच्छाथ मरुत इत्था विप्रं हवमानम् । मार्डीकेभिर्नाधमानम् ॥
8.7.e: When, Maruts, ye come to him, the singer who invokes you thus,  With favours to your suppliant?

8.7.d: कद्ध नूनं कधप्रियो यदिन्द्रमजहातन । को वः सखित्व ओहते ॥
8.7.e: What now? where have ye still a friend since ye left Indra all alone?  Who counteth on your friendship now?

8.7.d: सहो षु णो वज्रहस्तैः कण्वासो अग्निं मरुद्भिः । स्तुषे हिरण्यवाशीभिः ॥
8.7.e: The Kaṇvas sing forth Agni's praise together with our Maruts’ who  Wield thunder and wear swords of gold.

8.7.d: ओ षु वृष्णः प्रयज्यूना नव्यसे सुविताय । ववृत्यां चित्रवाजान् ॥
8.7.e: Hither for new felicity may I attract the Impetuous Ones,  The Heroes with their wondrous strength

8.7.d: गिरयश्चिन्नि जिहते पर्शानासो मन्यमानाः । पर्वताश्चिन्नि येमिरे ॥
8.7.e: Before them sink the very hills deerning themseives abysses: yea,  Even the mountains bend them down.

8.7.d: आक्ष्णयावानो वहन्त्यन्तरिक्षेण पततः । धातारः स्तुवते वयः ॥
8.7.e: Steeds flying on their tortuous path through mid-air carry them, and give  The man who lauds them strength and life.

8.7.d: अग्निर्हि जानि पूर्व्यश्छन्दो न सूरो अर्चिषा । ते भानुभिर्वि तस्थिरे ॥
8.7.e: Agni was born the first of all, like Sūrya lovely with his light:  With lustre these have spread abroad.

8.8.d: आ नो विश्वाभिरूतिभिरश्विना गच्छतं युवम् । दस्रा हिरण्यवर्तनी पिबतं सोम्यं मधु ॥
8.8.e: WITH all the succours that are yours, O Aśvins, hither come to us:  Wonderful, borne on paths of gold, drink ye the meath with Soma juice.

8.8.d: आ नूनं यातमश्विना रथेन सूर्यत्वचा । भुजी हिरण्यपेशसा कवी गम्भीरचेतसा ॥
8.8.e: Come now, ye Aśvins, on your car decked with a sun-bright canopy,  Bountiful, with your golden forms, Sages with depth of intellect.

8.8.d: आ यातं नहुषस्पर्यान्तरिक्षात्सुवृक्तिभिः । पिबाथो अश्विना मधु कण्वानां सवने सुतम् ॥
8.8.e: Come hither from the Nahusas, come, drawn by pure hymns, from mid-air.  O Aśvins, drink the savoury juice shed in the Kaṇvas' sacrifice.

8.8.d: आ नो यातं दिवस्पर्यान्तरिक्षादधप्रिया । पुत्रः कण्वस्य वामिह सुषाव सोम्यं मधु ॥
8.8.e: Come to us hither from the heavens, come from mid-air, well-loved by us:  Here Kaṇva's son hath pressed for you the pleasant meath of Soma juice.

8.8.d: आ नो यातमुपश्रुत्यश्विना सोमपीतये । स्वाहा स्तोमस्य वर्धना प्र कवी धीतिभिर्नरा ॥
8.8.e: Come, Aśvins, to give car to us, to drink the Soma, Aśvins, come.  Hail, Strengtheners of the praise-song speed onward, ye Heroes, with your thoughts.

8.8.d: यच्चिद्धि वां पुर ऋषयो जुहूरेऽवसे नरा । आ यातमश्विना गतमुपेमां सुष्टुतिं मम ॥
8.8.e: As, Heroes, in the olden time the Ṛṣis called you to their aid,  So now, O Aśvins, come to us, come near to this mine eulogy.

8.8.d: दिवश्चिद्रोचनादध्या नो गन्तं स्वर्विदा । धीभिर्वत्सप्रचेतसा स्तोमेभिर्हवनश्रुता ॥
8.8.e: Even from the luminous sphere of heaven come to us, ye who find the light,  Carers for Vatsa, through our prayers and lauds, O yewho hearour call.

8.8.d: किमन्ये पर्यासतेऽस्मत्स्तोमेभिरश्विना । पुत्रः कण्वस्य वामृषिर्गीर्भिर्वत्सो अवीवृधत् ॥
8.8.e: Do others more than we adore the Aśvins with their hymns of praise?  The Ṛṣi Vatsa, Kaṇva's son, hath magnified you with his songs.

8.8.d: आ वां विप्र इहावसेऽह्वत्स्तोमेभिरश्विना । अरिप्रा वृत्रहन्तमा ता नो भूतं मयोभुवा ॥
8.8.e: The holy singer with his hymns hath called you, Aśvins, hither-ward;  Best Vṛtra-slayers, free from stain, as such bring us felicity.

8.8.d: आ यद्वां योषणा रथमतिष्ठद्वाजिनीवसू । विश्वान्यश्विना युवं प्र धीतान्यगच्छतम् ॥
8.8.e: What time, ye Lords of ample wealth, the Lady mounted on your car,  Then, O ye Aśvins, ye attained all wishes that your hearts desired.

8.8.d: अतः सहस्रनिर्णिजा रथेना यातमश्विना । वत्सो वां मधुमद्वचोऽशंसीत्काव्यः कविः ॥
8.8.e: Come thence, O Aśvins, on your car that hath a thousand ornaments:  Vatsa the sage, the sage's son, hath sung a song of sweets to you.

8.8.d: पुरुमन्द्रा पुरूवसू मनोतरा रयीणाम् । स्तोमं मे अश्विनाविममभि वह्नी अनूषाताम् ॥
8.8.e: Cheerers of many, rich in goods, discoverers of opulence,  The Aśvins, Riders through the sky, have welcomed this my song of praise.

8.8.d: आ नो विश्वान्यश्विना धत्तं राधांस्यह्रया । कृतं न ऋत्वियावतो मा नो रीरधतं निदे ॥
8.8.e: O Aśvins, grant us all rich gifts wherewith no man mav interfere.  Make us observe the stated times: give us not over to reproach.

8.8.d: यन्नासत्या परावति यद्वा स्थो अध्यम्बरे । अतः सहस्रनिर्णिजा रथेना यातमश्विना ॥
8.8.e: Whether, Nāsatyas, ye be nigh, or whether ye be far away,  Come thence, O Aśvins, on your car that hath a thousand ornaments.

8.8.d: यो वां नासत्यावृषिर्गीर्भिर्वत्सो अवीवृधत् । तस्मै सहस्रनिर्णिजमिषं धत्तं घृतश्चुतम् ॥
8.8.e: Vatsa the Ṛṣi with his songs, Nāsatyas, hath exalted you:  Grant him rich food distilling oil, graced with a thousand ornaments.

8.8.d: प्रास्मा ऊर्जं घृतश्चुतमश्विना यच्छतं युवम् । यो वां सुम्नाय तुष्टवद्वसूयाद्दानुनस्पती ॥
8.8.e: Bestow on him, O Aśvins, food that strengthens, and that drops with oil,  On him who praises you for bliss, and, Lords of bounty, prays for wealth.

8.8.d: आ नो गन्तं रिशादसेमं स्तोमं पुरुभुजा । कृतं नः सुश्रियो नरेमा दातमभिष्टये ॥
8.8.e: Come to us, ye who slay the foe, Lords of rich treasure, to this hymn.  O Heroes, give us high renown and these good things of earth for help.

8.8.d: आ वां विश्वाभिरूतिभिः प्रियमेधा अहूषत । राजन्तावध्वराणामश्विना यामहूतिषु ॥
8.8.e: The Priyamedhas have invoked you with all succours that are yours,  You, Aśvins, Lords of solemn rites, with calls entreating you to come.

8.8.d: आ नो गन्तं मयोभुवाश्विना शम्भुवा युवम् । यो वां विपन्यू धीतिभिर्गीर्भिर्वत्सो अवीवृधत् ॥
8.8.e: Come to us, Aśvins, ye Who bring felicity, auspicious Ones,  To Vatsa who with prayer and hymn, lovers of song, hath honoured you.
